translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 121.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 121.

sentences.zh: 【宋紀三】起著雍執徐，盡上章敦牂，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Song Annals 3] From Zhuanyong Zhixu through Shangzhang Dunxiang; three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Song Annals 3] From Zhuanyong Zhixu through Shangzhang Dunxiang—three years in all.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝上之中元嘉五年（

translations.literal: The fifth year of Yuanjia, middle period of the first reign of Emperor Wen of Song (
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year of Yuanjia under the first reign of Emperor Wen of Song (

sentences.zh: 戊辰，公元四二八年）

translations.literal: wuchen, the year 428 CE)
translations.idiomatic: the year wuchen, 428 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛未，魏京兆王黎卒。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinwei, Li, Prince of Jingzhao of Wei, died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day xinwei, Li, Prince of Jingzhao of Northern Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史、彭城王義康，性聰察，在州職事修治。

translations.literal: Liu Yikang, Prince of Pengcheng, Governor of Jing Province, was intelligent and perceptive; in the province he administered affairs well.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yikang, Prince of Pengcheng and governor of Jing Province, was sharp-witted and perceptive, and ran provincial affairs effectively.

sentences.zh: 左光祿大夫范泰謂司徒王弘曰：「天下事重，權重難居。

translations.literal: Left Grandee of Splendid Happiness Fan Tai said to Minister-over-the-Masses Wang Hong: "The affairs of the realm weigh heavily; heavy authority is hard to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tai, Left Grandee of Splendid Happiness, said to Wang Hong, Minister-over-the-Masses: "The weight of the empire's business makes great power hard to bear.

sentences.zh: 卿兄弟盛滿，當深存降挹。

translations.literal: Your brothers' power is full to overflowing; you should deeply preserve humility and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Your house is at the height of its eminence; you must keep a deep measure of humility.

sentences.zh: 彭城王，帝之次弟，宜征還入朝，共參朝政。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Pengcheng is the emperor's next younger brother; he should be summoned back to court to take part in governing."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pengcheng is the emperor's next younger brother; summon him to court to share in government."

sentences.zh: 弘納其言。

translations.literal: Hong accepted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong took his advice.

sentences.zh: 時大旱，疾疫，弘上表引咎遜位，帝不許。

translations.literal: At this time there was great drought and epidemic disease; Hong submitted a memorial taking blame and yielding his post, but the emperor would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought and epidemic were raging; Hong memorialized the throne, accepting blame and offering to step down, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 秦商州刺史領澆河太守姚浚叛，降河西，秦王熾磐以尚書焦嵩代浚，帥騎三千討之。

translations.literal: Yao Jun, Governor of Shang Province of Qin and concurrent Administrator of Jiaohe, rebelled and surrendered to Hexi; King Chiqu of Qin appointed Minister of State Jiao Song to replace Jun and led three thousand horsemen to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Jun, Qin governor of Shang Province who also held Jiaohe commandery, rebelled and went over to Hexi; King Chiqu of Western Qin sent Jiao Song as his replacement and marched three thousand horse against him.

sentences.zh: 二月，嵩為吐谷渾元緒所執。

translations.literal: In the second month, Song was captured by Murong Yuanxu of Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Tuyuhun's Murong Yuanxu captured Song.

sentences.zh: 魏改元神䴥。

translations.literal: Wei changed the era name to Shengui.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei adopted the new era name Shengui.

sentences.zh: 魏平北將軍尉眷攻夏主於上邽，夏主退屯平涼。

translations.literal: Yu Juan, General Who Pacifies the North of Wei, attacked the Xia ruler at Shanggui; the Xia ruler withdrew and encamped at Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Juan, Northern Wei's General Who Pacifies the North, attacked the Xia ruler at Shanggui; the Xia ruler fell back to Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 奚斤進軍安定，與丘堆、娥清軍合。

translations.literal: Xi Jin advanced on Anding and joined forces with the armies of Qiu Dui and E Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin marched on Anding and united with the forces of Qiu Dui and E Qing.

sentences.zh: 斤馬多疫死，士卒乏糧，乃深壘自固。

translations.literal: Many of Jin's horses died of plague; the soldiers lacked grain, so they built deep ramparts and held fast.
translations.idiomatic: Plague killed many of Jin's horses and his men ran short of grain; he dug in behind deep fortifications.

sentences.zh: 遣丘堆督租於民間，士卒暴掠，不設儆備。

translations.literal: He sent Qiu Dui to levy grain among the people; the soldiers plundered violently and set no guard.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Qiu Dui to collect grain from the countryside; the troops looted at will and kept no watch.

sentences.zh: 夏主襲之，堆兵敗，以數百騎還城。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler raided him; Dui's army was defeated, and he returned to the city with only several hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler struck; Dui's force was routed, and he fled back to the city with only a few hundred riders.

sentences.zh: 夏主乘勝，日來城下鈔掠，不得芻牧，諸將患之。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler pressed his victory, coming daily beneath the walls to raid; they could not gather fodder or pasture livestock, and the generals were distressed.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler followed up, raiding under the walls day after day so that neither fodder nor grazing was possible; the Wei generals were deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 監軍侍御史安頡曰：「受詔滅賊，今更為賊所困，退守窮城，若不為賊殺，當坐法誅，進退皆無生理。

translations.literal: Supervising Army Attendant Censor An Gui said: "We received orders to destroy the rebels, yet now we are trapped by them instead, holding a desperate city. If the rebels do not kill us, we face execution by law—whether we advance or retreat there is no way to live.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Army Attendant Censor An Gui said: "We were ordered to destroy the enemy, yet now the enemy has us trapped in this doomed town. If they do not kill us, the law will—advance or retreat, there is no way out alive.

sentences.zh: 而諸王公晏然曾不為計乎？」

translations.literal: Yet do you lords and princes sit at ease and never plan for this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet you lords sit at ease as though none of this concerned you?"

sentences.zh: 斤曰：「今軍士無馬，以步擊騎，必無勝理，當須京師救騎至，合擊之。」

translations.literal: Jin said: "Now the army has no horses; infantry fighting cavalry can have no prospect of victory. We must wait until rescue cavalry arrives from the capital, then strike together."
translations.idiomatic: Jin replied: "Our men have no horses; foot soldiers cannot beat cavalry. We must wait for relief horse from the capital and attack together."

sentences.zh: 頡曰：「今猛寇游逸於外，吾兵疲食盡，不一決戰，則殆在旦夕，救騎何可待乎！

translations.literal: Gui said: "Now the fierce enemy roams freely outside while our troops are exhausted and our food is gone. If we do not fight a decisive battle, we are doomed within days—how can we wait for rescue cavalry!
translations.idiomatic: Gui said: "The enemy roams at will while we are spent and starving. Without a decisive battle we perish within days—how can we wait for reinforcements?

sentences.zh: 等於就死，死戰，不亦可乎！」

translations.literal: It is the same as courting death—why not die fighting!"
translations.idiomatic: Waiting is death anyway—why not die in battle?"

sentences.zh: 斤又以馬少為辭。

translations.literal: Jin again pleaded the shortage of horses.
translations.idiomatic: Jin again objected that they had too few horses.

sentences.zh: 頡曰：「今斂諸將所乘馬，可得二百匹，頡請募敢死之士出擊之，就不能破敵，亦可以折其銳。

translations.literal: Gui said: "If we gather the horses the generals ride, we can obtain two hundred. I ask to recruit dare-to-die men to strike out. Even if we cannot break the enemy, we can blunt their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Gui said: "Collect every general's mount and we can muster two hundred horses. Let me raise a suicide squad and strike. Even if we do not rout them, we can blunt their momentum.

sentences.zh: 且赫連昌狷而無謀，好勇而輕，每自出挑戰，眾皆識之。

translations.literal: Moreover Helian Chang is narrow-minded and without strategy, brave but rash; he personally comes out to challenge battle each time, and all recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Helian Chang is headstrong and unwise, bold but reckless; he comes out to challenge us in person every time, and every man knows his face.

sentences.zh: 若伏兵掩擊，昌可擒也。」

translations.literal: If we set an ambush and strike by surprise, Chang can be captured."
translations.idiomatic: With an ambush we can take Chang alive."

sentences.zh: 斤猶難之。

translations.literal: Jin still hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: Jin still held back.

sentences.zh: 頡乃陰與尉眷等謀，選騎待之。

translations.literal: Gui then secretly plotted with Yu Juan and the others, selecting horsemen and waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Gui secretly coordinated with Yu Juan and the others, picked their riders, and lay in wait.

sentences.zh: 既而夏主來攻城，頡出應之。

translations.literal: Presently the Xia ruler came to attack the city; Gui went out to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia ruler came to assault the walls, Gui rode out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 夏主自出陳前搏戰，軍士識其貌，爭赴之。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler personally came forward to fight in the van; the soldiers recognized his face and rushed toward him.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler fought in the front rank himself; the Wei soldiers knew his face and surged toward him.

sentences.zh: 會天大風，揚塵，晝昏，夏主財走，頡追之，夏主馬蹶而墜，遂擒之。

translations.literal: Just then a great wind arose, raising dust until day turned dim; the Xia ruler had just fled when Gui pursued him; the Xia ruler's horse stumbled and fell, and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce wind whipped up dust until broad day turned dark; the Xia ruler had barely fled when Gui overtook him; his horse stumbled and threw him, and he was taken.

sentences.zh: 夏大將軍、領司徒、平原王定收其餘眾數萬，奔還平涼，即皇帝位，大赦，改元勝光。

translations.literal: Helian Ding, Great General of Xia, concurrent Minister of State, Prince of Pingyuan, gathered the remaining tens of thousands and fled back to Pingliang, where he took the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Shengguang.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Ding, Xia's great general and Prince of Pingyuan, rallied tens of thousands of survivors and fled to Pingliang, where he proclaimed himself emperor, granted a general amnesty, and adopted the era name Shengguang.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛巳，赫連昌至平城，魏主館之於西宮，門內器用皆給乘輿之副，又以妹始平公主妻之；

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinsi, Helian Chang arrived at Pingcheng; the Wei emperor lodged him in the Western Palace, furnishing the gates and inner quarters with duplicates of the imperial equipage, and gave him his sister Princess Shiping in marriage;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day xinsi, Helian Chang reached Pingcheng; the Wei emperor housed him in the Western Palace with furnishings matching the imperial standard and married him to his sister, Princess Shiping;

sentences.zh: 假常忠將軍，賜爵會稽公。

translations.literal: he was given the acting title General of Constant Loyalty and enfeoffed as Duke of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: he was named acting General of Constant Loyalty and created Duke of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 以安頡為建節將軍，賜爵西平公；

translations.literal: An Gui was made General Who Establishes Authority and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiping;
translations.idiomatic: An Gui was appointed General Who Establishes Authority and created Duke of Xiping;

sentences.zh: 尉眷為寧北將軍，進爵漁陽公。

translations.literal: Yu Juan was made General Who Pacifies the North and advanced to Duke of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Juan was named General Who Pacifies the North and advanced to Duke of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 魏主常使赫連昌侍從左右，與之單騎共逐鹿，深入山澗。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor often had Helian Chang attend at his side, riding alone with him to hunt deer deep into mountain ravines.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor often kept Helian Chang at his side, riding out alone with him to hunt deer far into the hills.

sentences.zh: 昌素有勇名，諸將威以為不可。

translations.literal: Chang had long borne a name for valor; the generals all thought this unsafe.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was famous for his courage; the generals all protested that this was too dangerous.

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「天命有在，亦何所懼！」

translations.literal: The Wei emperor said: "When the Mandate of Heaven is with one, what is there to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor said: "Heaven's mandate rests with me—what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 親遇如初。

translations.literal: He treated him with personal favor as at first.
translations.idiomatic: He treated him with the same personal favor as before.

sentences.zh: 奚斤自以為元帥，而昌為偏裨所擒，深恥之。

translations.literal: Xi Jin regarded himself as supreme commander, yet Chang had been captured by a subordinate officer; he was deeply shamed.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin was supreme commander, yet a junior officer had captured Chang; the shame cut deep.

sentences.zh: 乃捨輜重，繼三日糧，追夏主於平涼。

translations.literal: He abandoned the baggage train, took only three days' grain, and pursued the Xia ruler to Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: He left the baggage train behind, carried only three days' rations, and pursued the Xia ruler toward Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 娥清欲循水而往，斤不從，自北道邀其走路。

translations.literal: E Qing wished to go by following the water, but Jin would not agree and instead took the northern road to intercept the Xia ruler's line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: E Qing wanted to advance along the river, but Jin refused and took the northern route to cut off the Xia ruler's retreat.

sentences.zh: 至馬髦嶺，夏軍將遁，會魏小將有罪亡歸於夏，告以魏軍食少無水。

translations.literal: When they reached Mamiao Ridge the Xia army was about to flee, when a minor Wei officer who had fled to Xia for a crime reported that the Wei army had little food and no water.
translations.idiomatic: At Mamiao Ridge the Xia army was on the verge of escape when a minor Wei officer who had defected to Xia for a crime reported that the Wei force was short of food and water.

sentences.zh: 夏主乃分兵邀斤，前後夾擊之，魏兵大潰，斤及娥清、劉拔皆為夏所擒，士卒死者六七千人。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler then divided his forces to intercept Jin and attacked from front and rear; the Wei army was routed in great defeat. Jin, E Qing, and Liu Ba were all captured by Xia, and six or seven thousand soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler split his force to ambush Jin and struck from both sides; the Wei army collapsed. Jin, E Qing, and Liu Ba were all taken, and six or seven thousand men were killed.

sentences.zh: 丘堆守輜重在安定，聞斤敗，棄輜重奔長安，與高涼王禮偕奔薄阪，夏人復取長安。

translations.literal: Qiu Dui was guarding the baggage at Anding; hearing of Jin's defeat, he abandoned the train and fled to Chang'an, then fled with Prince Li of Gaoliang to Bofan together; the Xia people recovered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Dui was guarding the baggage at Anding; when he heard of Jin's defeat he abandoned it and fled to Chang'an, then fled with Prince Li of Gaoliang to Bofan; Xia recovered Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 魏主大怒，命安頡斬丘堆，代將其眾，鎮薄阪以拒之。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor was greatly enraged and ordered An Gui to execute Qiu Dui, take command of his troops in his stead, and garrison Bofan to resist the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor was furious; he ordered An Gui to execute Qiu Dui, assume his command, and hold Bofan against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，夏主遣使請和於魏，魏主以詔諭之使降。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the Xia ruler sent envoys to seek peace with Wei; the Wei emperor issued an edict instructing him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, the Xia ruler sent envoys to sue for peace; the Wei emperor replied with an edict demanding his surrender.

sentences.zh: 壬子，魏主西巡。

translations.literal: On renzi the Wei emperor toured west.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renzi the Wei emperor made a western tour.

sentences.zh: 戊午，畋於河西。

translations.literal: On wuwu he hunted west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuwu he hunted west of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 大赦。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 五月，秦文昭王熾磐卒，太子暮末即位，大赦，改元永弘。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Chiqu, the Cultured and Illustrious King of Qin, died; the crown prince Mumo succeeded, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yonghong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month King Chiqu of Western Qin died; the crown prince Mumo succeeded, granted a general amnesty, and adopted the era name Yonghong.

sentences.zh: 平陸令河南成粲復勸王弘遜位，弘從之，累表陳請。

translations.literal: Cheng Can of Henan, magistrate of Pinglu, again urged Wang Hong to yield his post; Hong agreed and submitted repeated memorials requesting it.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Can of Henan, magistrate of Pinglu, again urged Wang Hong to step down; Hong agreed and memorialized repeatedly to that effect.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，六月，庚戌，以弘為衛將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: The emperor, having no choice, in the sixth month on gengxu appointed Hong General of the Guard with the Bountiful Rites Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, left no choice, in the sixth month on the day gengxu named Hong General of the Guard with Bountiful Rites Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，魏主如長川。

translations.literal: On jiayin the Wei emperor went to Changchuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiayin the Wei emperor went to Changchuan.

sentences.zh: 葬秦文昭王於武平陵，廟號太祖。

translations.literal: The Cultured and Illustrious King of Qin was buried at Wuping Mausoleum; his temple name was Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: The late king was buried at Wuping Mausoleum with the temple name Taizu.

sentences.zh: 秦王暮末以右丞相元基為侍中、相國、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，以鎮軍大將軍、河州牧謙屯為驃騎大將軍，征安北將軍、涼州刺史段暉為輔國大將軍、御史大夫，叔父右禁將軍千年為鎮北將軍、涼州牧，鎮湟河，以征北將軍木弈干為尚書令、車騎大將軍，以征南將軍吉毘為尚書僕射、衛大將軍。

translations.literal: King Mumo of Qin appointed Right Chancellor Yuanji Palace Attendant, Chancellor of State, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing; made Qiantun, General Who Guards the Army and Governor of He Province, General of Agile Cavalry; made Duan Hui, General Who Campaigns Against the North and Governor of Liang Province, General Who Assists the State and Grand Censor; made his uncle Qiannian, Right General of the Forbidden Guard, General Who Guards the North and Governor of Liang Province, to garrison Huanghe; made Muyigan, General Who Campaigns Against the North, Minister of State and General of Chariots and Cavalry; and made Jipi, General Who Campaigns Against the South, Vice Minister of State and General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: King Mumo appointed Yuanji, his right chancellor, Palace Attendant, Chancellor of State, supreme commander, and chief of the secretariat; Qiantun became General of Agile Cavalry; Duan Hui, governor of Liang, became General Who Assists the State and Grand Censor; his uncle Qiannian became General Who Guards the North and governor of Liang, stationed at Huanghe; Muyigan became Minister of State and General of Chariots and Cavalry; and Jipi became Vice Minister and General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜因秦喪，伐秦西平。

translations.literal: Mengxun, King of Hexi, took advantage of Qin's mourning to attack Xiping of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun, king of Hexi, exploited Western Qin's mourning to attack Xiping.

sentences.zh: 西平太守麴承謂之曰：「殿下若先取樂都，則西平必為殿下之有。

translations.literal: Qu Cheng, Administrator of Xiping, said to him: "If Your Highness first takes Ledu, then Xiping will surely be yours.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Cheng, administrator of Xiping, told him: "If you take Ledu first, Xiping will fall into your hands.

sentences.zh: 西平苟望風請服，亦明主之所疾也。」

translations.literal: If Xiping merely submits at the rumor of your approach, that too is what a wise ruler should disdain."
translations.idiomatic: A city that surrenders at mere rumor is not worth a wise ruler's pride."

sentences.zh: 蒙遜乃釋西平，攻樂都。

translations.literal: Mengxun then released Xiping and attacked Ledu.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun left Xiping and marched on Ledu.

sentences.zh: 相國元基帥騎三千救樂都，甫入城，而河西兵至，攻其外城，克之；

translations.literal: Chancellor Yuanji led three thousand horsemen to relieve Ledu; he had just entered the city when Hexi troops arrived, attacked the outer city, and took it;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yuanji rode three thousand horse to relieve Ledu; he had barely entered when Hexi troops arrived, stormed the outer city, and took it;

sentences.zh: 絕其水道，城中飢渴，死者太半。

translations.literal: they cut off the water supply; within the city hunger and thirst raged, and more than half died.
translations.idiomatic: they cut the water supply; famine and thirst killed more than half the garrison.

sentences.zh: 東羌乞提從元基救樂都，陰與河西通謀，下繩引內其兵，登城者百餘人，鼓噪燒門；

translations.literal: Qiti of the Eastern Qiang, who had accompanied Yuanji to relieve Ledu, secretly conspired with Hexi, lowered ropes to draw their soldiers in, and more than a hundred climbed the walls, beating drums, shouting, and burning the gates;
translations.idiomatic: Qiti of the Eastern Qiang, who had marched with Yuanji, secretly colluded with Hexi, lowered ropes to admit their troops, and more than a hundred scaled the walls, shouting and setting fire to the gates;

sentences.zh: 元基帥左右奮擊，河西兵乃退。

translations.literal: Yuanji led his personal guard in a fierce counterattack, and the Hexi troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji led his household guard in a fierce counterattack and drove the Hexi troops back.

sentences.zh: 初，文昭王疾病，謂暮末曰：「吾死之後，汝能保境則善矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Cultured and Illustrious King was ill, he said to Mumo: "After I die, if you can hold the borders that will be well enough.
translations.idiomatic: When the late king lay ill he told Mumo: "After I am gone, merely holding our borders will be achievement enough.

sentences.zh: 沮渠成都為蒙遜所親重，汝宜歸之。」

translations.literal: Juqu Chengdu is held dear by Mengxun; you should submit to him."
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Chengdu is favored by Mengxun; you should submit to him."

sentences.zh: 至是，暮末遣使詣蒙遜，許歸成都以求和。

translations.literal: Now Mumo sent envoys to Mengxun, promising to return Chengdu to seek peace.
translations.idiomatic: Mumo now sent envoys to Mengxun, offering to return Chengdu in exchange for peace.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜引兵還，遣使入秦弔祭。

translations.literal: Mengxun withdrew his army and sent envoys into Qin to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun withdrew and sent envoys to Qin to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 暮末厚資送成都，遣將軍王伐送之。

translations.literal: Mumo richly provisioned Chengdu's escort and sent General Wang Fa to conduct him.
translations.idiomatic: Mumo sent Chengdu back with rich gifts and dispatched General Wang Fa as escort.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜猶疑之，使恢武將軍沮渠奇珍伏兵於捫天嶺，執伐並其騎士三百人以歸。

translations.literal: Mengxun still harbored doubts and had Juqu Qizhen, General Who Restores Martial Glory, set an ambush at Mentian Ridge, seizing Fa and his three hundred horsemen and bringing them back.
translations.idiomatic: Still suspicious, Mengxun had Juqu Qizhen, General Who Restores Martial Glory, ambush them at Mentian Ridge, seized Wang Fa and his three hundred riders, and brought them in.

sentences.zh: 既而遣尚書郎王杼送伐還秦，並遺暮末馬千匹及錦罽銀繒。

translations.literal: Presently he sent Master of Writing Attendant Wang Zhu to return Fa to Qin, and also sent Mumo a thousand horses together with brocade, felt, silver, and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Master of Writing Wang Zhu to return Fa to Qin and presented Mumo with a thousand horses, brocades, felts, silver, and silks.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，暮末遣記室郎中馬艾如河西報聘。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Mumo sent Recorder Attendant Ma Ai to Hexi on a return visit.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Mumo sent Ma Ai to Hexi on a return embassy.

sentences.zh: 魏主還宮。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor returned to court.

sentences.zh: 八月，復如廣寧觀溫泉。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he again went to Guangning to view the hot springs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he again went to Guangning to visit the hot springs.

sentences.zh: 柔然紇升蓋可汗遣其子將萬餘騎寇魏邊。

translations.literal: Heshenggai Khan of Rouran sent his son with more than ten thousand horsemen to raid the Wei frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Heshenggai Khan of Rouran sent his son at the head of more than ten thousand horse to raid the Wei border.

sentences.zh: 魏主自廣寧還，追之，不及。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor returned from Guangning and pursued them but did not overtake them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor returned from Guangning in pursuit but could not catch them.

sentences.zh: 九月，還宮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲辰，魏主北巡。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiachen, the Wei emperor toured north.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jiachen, the Wei emperor made a northern tour.

sentences.zh: 壬子，畋於牛川。

translations.literal: On renzi he hunted at Niuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renzi he hunted at Niuchuan.

sentences.zh: 秦涼州牧乞伏千年，嗜酒殘虐，不恤政事，秦王暮未遣使讓之，千年懼，奔河西。

translations.literal: Qifu Qiannian, Governor of Liang Province of Qin, was addicted to wine, cruel and violent, and heedless of government; King Mumo of Qin sent envoys to reprove him; Qiannian was afraid and fled to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Qiannian, Western Qin's governor of Liang, drank heavily, ruled with cruelty, and neglected affairs; Mumo sent envoys to rebuke him; terrified, Qiannian fled to Hexi.

sentences.zh: 暮末以叔父光祿大夫沃陵為涼州牧，鎮湟河。

translations.literal: Mumo appointed his uncle Woling, Grandee of Splendid Happiness, Governor of Liang Province to garrison Huanghe.
translations.idiomatic: Mumo appointed his uncle Woling, Grandee of Splendid Happiness, governor of Liang and stationed him at Huanghe.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史王仲德遣步騎二千伐魏濟陽、陳留。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongde, Governor of Xu Province, sent two thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Jiyang and Chenliu of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongde, governor of Xu Province, sent two thousand foot and horse against Wei's Jiyang and Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 魏主還宮。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor returned to court.

sentences.zh: 魏定州丁零鮮于台陽第二千餘家叛，入西山，州郡不能討。

translations.literal: More than two thousand households of the Dingling Xianyu Taiyangdi of Ding Province of Wei rebelled, entered the western hills, and the province and commanderies could not suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: More than two thousand Dingling households led by Xianyu Taiyangdi in Ding Province rebelled, fled into the western hills, and local authorities could not suppress them.

sentences.zh: 閏月，魏主遣鎮南將軍叔孫建討之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month the Wei emperor sent Tushujian, General Who Guards the South, to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month the Wei emperor sent Tushujian, General Who Guards the South, against them.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day yimao, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the new moon of yimao, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 魏主如西河校獵。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor went to Xihe to conduct a military hunt.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor went to Xihe for a military hunt.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲申，還宮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiashen, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day jiashen, he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜伐秦，至磐夷，秦相國元基等將騎萬五千拒之。

translations.literal: Mengxun, King of Hexi, attacked Qin and reached Panyi; Chancellor Yuanji and others of Qin led fifteen thousand horsemen to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun attacked Western Qin and advanced to Panyi; Chancellor Yuanji and others met him with fifteen thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜還攻西平，征虜將軍出連輔政等將騎二千救之。

translations.literal: Mengxun turned back to attack Xiping; Chilian Fuzheng, General Who Campaigns Against Barbarians, and others led two thousand horsemen to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun turned on Xiping; Chilian Fuzheng, General Who Campaigns Against Barbarians, rode two thousand horse to its relief.

sentences.zh: 秘書監謝靈運，自以名輩才能，應參時政。

translations.literal: Xie Lingyun, Director of the Secretariat, considered himself by fame and generation and by talent fit to take part in governing.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lingyun, Director of the Secretariat, believed that by reputation, seniority, and talent he ought to share in government.

sentences.zh: 上唯接以文義，每侍宴談賞而已。

translations.literal: The emperor received him only on grounds of literary culture, having him attend banquets for talk and appreciation of writing, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received him only as a man of letters, keeping him at banquets for literary conversation and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 王曇首、王華、殷景仁名位素出靈運下，並見任遇，靈運意甚不平，多稱疾不朝直；

translations.literal: Wang Tanzhou, Wang Hua, and Yin Jingren had always ranked below Lingyun in fame and position, yet all received appointment and favor; Lingyun was deeply resentful and often pleaded illness and did not attend court duty;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanzhou, Wang Hua, and Yin Jingren had always ranked below him, yet all held office and favor; Lingyun was bitter and often pleaded illness to avoid court duty;

sentences.zh: 或出郭遊行，且二百里，經旬不歸，既無表聞，又不請急。

translations.literal: sometimes he went outside the walls on pleasure trips as far as two hundred li, not returning for ten days or more, neither notifying the throne by memorial nor requesting leave for urgent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: sometimes he wandered beyond the suburbs as far as two hundred li and stayed away ten days or more without memorializing the throne or requesting leave.

sentences.zh: 上不欲傷大臣意，諷令自解。

translations.literal: The emperor did not wish to wound a great minister's feelings and hinted that he should resign of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to wound a senior minister openly, the emperor hinted that he should resign.

sentences.zh: 靈運乃上表陳疾，上賜假，令還會稽。

translations.literal: Lingyun then submitted a memorial stating illness; the emperor granted leave and ordered him to return to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun memorialized his illness; the emperor granted leave and sent him back to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 而靈運游飲自若，為法司所糾，坐免官。

translations.literal: Yet Lingyun went on drinking and roaming as before and was impeached by the judicial authorities; he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lingyun continued to drink and roam as though nothing had changed; the judicial authorities impeached him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，師子王剎利摩訶及天竺迦毘黎王月愛，皆遣使奉表入貢，表辭皆如浮屠之言。

translations.literal: That year the Lion King Shalimoke and the King of Kapili in India, Chandramukha, both sent envoys with memorials and tribute; the wording of the memorials was all in the manner of Buddhist speech.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Lion King Shalimoke and Kapili's King Chandramukha in India both sent envoys with tribute; their memorials were couched entirely in Buddhist idiom.

sentences.zh: 魏鎮遠將軍平舒侯燕鳳卒。

translations.literal: Yan Feng, Marquis of Pingshu and General Who Guards the Distance of Wei, died.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Feng, Marquis of Pingshu and Wei's General Who Guards the Distance, died.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝上之中元嘉六年（

translations.literal: The sixth year of Yuanjia, middle period of the first reign of Emperor Wen of Song (
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year of Yuanjia under the first reign of Emperor Wen of Song (

sentences.zh: 己巳，公元四二九年）

translations.literal: jisi, the year 429 CE)
translations.idiomatic: the year jisi, 429 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，王弘上表乞解州、錄，以授彭城王義康，帝優詔不許。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Wang Hong submitted a memorial requesting to relinquish his provincial and recording duties and transfer them to the Prince of Pengcheng Yikang; the emperor issued a gracious edict refusing.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Wang Hong asked to surrender his provincial and secretariat duties to the Prince of Pengcheng Yikang; the emperor graciously refused.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以義康為侍中、都督揚、南徐、袞三州諸軍事、司徒、錄尚書事、領南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On guichou Yikang was made Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of the Armies of Yang, Southern Xu, and Yan Provinces, Minister of State, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and concurrent Governor of Southern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guichou Yikang was named Palace Attendant, supreme commander of Yang, Southern Xu, and Yan, Minister of State, chief of the secretariat, and governor of Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 弘與義康二府並置佐領兵，共輔朝政。

translations.literal: Hong and Yikang each established staffs with assistants leading troops, jointly assisting court governance.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and Yikang each maintained staffs with military aides and together assisted the government.

sentences.zh: 弘既多疾，且欲委遠大權，每事推讓義康，由是義康專總內外之務。

translations.literal: Hong was often ill and wished to delegate great authority; on every matter he yielded to Yikang, so that Yikang came to monopolize affairs within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was frequently ill and wished to shed heavy responsibility; he deferred to Yikang on every matter, and Yikang came to control all affairs, civil and military.

sentences.zh: 又以撫將軍江夏王義恭為都督荊、湘等八州諸軍事、荊州刺史，以待中劉湛為南蠻校尉，行府州事。

translations.literal: He also made Liu Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia and General Who Pacifies, Commander-in-Chief of the Armies of Jing, Xiang, and six other provinces and Governor of Jing Province, and made Palace Attendant Liu Zhan Colonel of the Southern Man and acting administrator of the princely fief and province.
translations.idiomatic: He also named Liu Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, commander of Jing, Xiang, and six other provinces and governor of Jing, and made Palace Attendant Liu Zhan Colonel of the Southern Man with charge of the princely establishment and province.

sentences.zh: 帝與義恭書，誡之曰：「天下艱難，家國事重，雖曰守成，實亦未易。

translations.literal: The emperor wrote to Yigong admonishing him: "The realm is hard pressed; the affairs of house and state weigh heavily. Though one speaks of preserving what is established, in truth it is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote Yigong a letter of admonition: "The realm is in difficulty and the weight of house and state is great. Preserving what has been won sounds simple; it is not.

sentences.zh: 隆替安危，在吾曹耳，豈可不感尋王業，大懼負荷！

translations.literal: Rise and fall, safety and peril, rest on us—how can we fail to reflect on the royal enterprise and greatly fear the burden we bear!
translations.idiomatic: Whether the dynasty rises or falls rests on us—how can we fail to ponder the royal enterprise and dread the burden we bear!

sentences.zh: 汝性褊急，志之所滯，其欲必行，意所不存，從物回改。

translations.literal: Your nature is narrow and hasty; where your will is fixed you must have your way, and where your mind is not engaged you bend with others.
translations.idiomatic: You are narrow and impulsive: what you fix your mind on you insist on, and what does not interest you abandon at others' urging.

sentences.zh: 此最弊事，宜念裁抑。

translations.literal: This is the greatest fault; you should think on it and restrain yourself.
translations.idiomatic: This is your worst fault; remember it and restrain yourself.

sentences.zh: 衛表遇士大夫以禮，與小人有恩；

translations.literal: Wei Biao treated gentlemen with courtesy yet showed kindness to petty men;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Biao treated gentlemen with courtesy yet showed kindness to petty men;

sentences.zh: 西門、安於，矯性齊美；

translations.literal: Ximen and An Yu bent their natures to equal excellence;
translations.idiomatic: Ximen and An Yu bent their natures toward equal excellence;

sentences.zh: 關羽、張飛，任偏同弊。

translations.literal: Guan Yu and Zhang Fei indulged partiality to the same harm.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu and Zhang Fei indulged partiality to the same ruin.

sentences.zh: 行己舉事，深宜鑒此！

translations.literal: In your conduct and actions you should deeply take this as a mirror!
translations.idiomatic: In your conduct and actions take these as your mirror!

sentences.zh: 若事異今日，嗣子幼蒙，司徒當周公之事，汝不可不盡祗順之理。

translations.literal: If affairs differ from today and the heir is young and untutored, the Minister of State will perform the Duke of Zhou's role; you must not fail in the duty of reverent obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Should the day come when the heir is young, the Minister of State will play the Duke of Zhou's part; you must observe every rule of reverent obedience.

sentences.zh: 爾時天下安危，決汝二人耳。

translations.literal: At that time the safety or peril of the realm will be decided by you two alone.
translations.idiomatic: Then the fate of the realm will rest on you two alone.

sentences.zh: 「汝一月自用錢不可過三十萬，若能省此，益美。

translations.literal: Your personal monthly expenditure must not exceed three hundred thousand; if you can reduce this, so much the better.
translations.idiomatic: Your personal spending must not exceed three hundred thousand cash a month; less would be better still.

sentences.zh: 西楚府捨，略所諳究，計當不須改作，日求新異。

translations.literal: The buildings of the Western Chu princely establishment are roughly adequate to what you need; they should not require rebuilding while you daily seek novelty.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Chu residence is adequate as it stands; do not rebuild it while chasing daily novelty.

sentences.zh: 凡訊獄多決當時，難可逆慮，此實為難。

translations.literal: In general trials are mostly decided on the spot; it is hard to foresee in advance—this is truly difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Trials are usually decided on the spot, which makes foresight hard—this is genuinely difficult.

sentences.zh: 至訊日，虛懷博盡，慎無以喜怒加人。

translations.literal: On the day of interrogation, open your mind and hear all fully; take care not to visit your joy or anger upon others.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of trial, listen with an open mind; do not let mood dictate your treatment of others.

sentences.zh: 能擇善者而從之，美自歸己；

translations.literal: If you can choose the good and follow it, the credit will be yours;
translations.idiomatic: Choose the good and follow it, and the credit will be yours;

sentences.zh: 不可專意自決，以矜獨斷之明也！

translations.literal: you must not decide everything yourself to flaunt the brilliance of sole judgment!
translations.idiomatic: do not decide everything yourself to flaunt your own judgment!

sentences.zh: 名器深宜慎惜，不可妄以假人。

translations.literal: Titles and insignia should be deeply cherished and not rashly bestowed on others.
translations.idiomatic: Titles and insignia must be guarded carefully and not given away lightly.

sentences.zh: 暱近爵賜，尤應裁量。

translations.literal: Enfeoffments and gifts to intimates especially require measure.
translations.idiomatic: Grants to favorites especially require restraint.

sentences.zh: 吾於左右雖為少恩，如聞外論不以為非也。

translations.literal: Though I show little favor to those close at hand, I hear that outside opinion does not regard this as wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am sparing with those close at hand, I hear that public opinion does not fault me for it.

sentences.zh: 以貴凌物，物不服；

translations.literal: When the noble bully others, others will not submit;
translations.idiomatic: Bully others with rank and they will not submit;

sentences.zh: 以威加人，人不厭；

translations.literal: when authority is forced on others, others will not be satisfied;
translations.idiomatic: force authority on others and they will resent it;

sentences.zh: 此易達事耳。

translations.literal: these are easy matters to understand.
translations.idiomatic: these are easy truths to grasp.

sentences.zh: 「聲樂嬉游，不宜令過；

translations.literal: Music and diversions should not be allowed to excess;
translations.idiomatic: Music and diversions must not be indulged to excess;

sentences.zh: 蒲酒漁獵，一切勿為。

translations.literal: gambling, wine, fishing, and hunting—you must do none of these.
translations.idiomatic: gambling, heavy drinking, fishing, and hunting—forbid them all.

sentences.zh: 供用奉身，皆有節度，奇服異器，不宜興長。

translations.literal: Supplies for personal use should all have limits; strange garments and unusual implements should not be encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Personal expenses must stay within bounds; do not encourage exotic dress or curios.

sentences.zh: 又宜數引見佐史。

translations.literal: You should also frequently summon your staff clerks to audience.
translations.idiomatic: Summon your staff clerks frequently.

sentences.zh: 相見不數，則彼我不親；

translations.literal: If you do not meet often, you and they will not be close;
translations.idiomatic: Without frequent meetings you and they will not be close;

sentences.zh: 不親，無因得盡人情；

translations.literal: without closeness there is no means to know men's hearts fully;
translations.idiomatic: without closeness you cannot know men's hearts;

sentences.zh: 人情不盡，復何由知眾事也！」

translations.literal: if hearts are not fully known, how then can you know the multitude of affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: if you do not know men's hearts, how can you know the affairs of the realm!"

sentences.zh: 夏酒泉公俊自平涼奔魏。

translations.literal: Jun, Duke of Jiuquan of Xia, fled from Pingliang to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, Duke of Jiuquan of Xia, fled from Pingliang to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 丁零鮮于台陽等請降於魏，魏主赦之。

translations.literal: Xianyu Taiyangdi of the Dingling and others sought surrender to Wei; the Wei emperor pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Taiyangdi of the Dingling and others surrendered to Wei and were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 秦出連輔政等未至西平，河西王蒙遜拔西平，執太守麴承。

translations.literal: Chilian Fuzheng and others of Qin had not yet reached Xiping when Mengxun, King of Hexi, took Xiping and seized Administrator Qu Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Before Chilian Fuzheng and the Western Qin relief force reached Xiping, Mengxun took the city and seized Qu Cheng, its administrator.

sentences.zh: 二月，秦王暮末立妃梁氏為王后，子萬載為太子。

translations.literal: In the second month King Mumo of Qin made Lady Liang queen and his son Wanzai crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Mumo made Lady Liang his queen and his son Wanzai crown prince.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁巳，立丘子劭為太子。

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingsi, his son Shao was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day dingsi, his son Shao was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 戊午，大赦。

translations.literal: On wuwu a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuwu he proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以左衛將軍殷景仁為中領軍。

translations.literal: On xinyou Yin Jingren, General of the Left Guard, was made Central Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinyou Yin Jingren, General of the Left Guard, was named Central Army Commander.

sentences.zh: 帝以章太后早亡；

translations.literal: Because Empress Dowager Zhang had died early,
translations.idiomatic: Because Empress Dowager Zhang had died young,

sentences.zh: 奉太后所生蘇氏甚謹。

translations.literal: the emperor had served the birth mother of the empress dowager, Lady Su, with great care.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor had cared devotedly for the empress dowager's birth mother, Lady Su.

sentences.zh: 蘇氏卒，帝往臨哭，欲追加封爵，使群臣議之。

translations.literal: When Lady Su died the emperor went to mourn at her bier and wished to add posthumous enfeoffment, ordering the ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Su died the emperor went to mourn and wished to grant her posthumous rank; he ordered the ministers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 景仁以為古典無之，乃止。

translations.literal: Jingren held that antiquity provided no precedent for this, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren argued that antiquity offered no precedent, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 初，秦尚書隴西辛進從文昭王游陵霄觀，彈飛鳥，誤中秦王暮末之母，傷其面。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xin Jin of Longxi, Minister of State of Qin, while accompanying the Cultured and Illustrious King on an outing to Lingxiao Terrace, shot at birds and by mistake struck the mother of King Mumo of Qin, wounding her face.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xin Jin of Longxi, a Qin minister, was shooting birds with the late king at Lingxiao Terrace and accidentally struck Mumo's mother in the face.

sentences.zh: 及暮末即位，問母面傷之由，母以狀告。

translations.literal: When Mumo took the throne he asked how his mother's face had been injured; his mother told him what had happened.
translations.idiomatic: When Mumo succeeded he asked how his mother's face had been scarred; she told him the story.

sentences.zh: 暮末怒，殺進，並其五族二十七人。

translations.literal: Mumo was enraged and killed Jin, together with twenty-seven people of his five clans.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Mumo executed Jin and twenty-seven members of his five clans.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸亥，以尚書左射王敬弘為尚書令，臨川王義慶為左僕射，吏部尚書濟陽江夷為右僕射。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on guihai, Wang Jinghong, Left Master of Writing, was made Minister of State; Liu Yiqing, Prince of Linchuan, was made Left Vice Minister; Jiang Yi of Jiyang, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, was made Right Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day guihai, Wang Jinghong became Minister of State, the Prince of Linchuan became Left Vice Minister, and Jiang Yi of Jiyang became Right Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 初，魏太祖命尚書郎鄧淵撰《國記》十餘卷，未成而止。

translations.literal: Earlier the Taizu of Wei had ordered Master of Writing Attendant Deng Yuan to compile more than ten juan of the National Chronicle, but it was unfinished when work stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Taizu of Wei had ordered Deng Yuan to compile more than ten juan of a National Chronicle, but the work was left unfinished.

sentences.zh: 世祖更命崔浩與中書侍郎鄧穎等續成之，為《國書》三十卷。

translations.literal: Shizu again ordered Cui Hao together with Secretariat Attendant Deng Ying and others to continue and complete it, producing thirty juan of the National Book.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu ordered Cui Hao, Deng Ying, and others to finish it, producing thirty juan of the National Book.

sentences.zh: 穎，淵之子也。

translations.literal: Ying was Yuan's son.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was Deng Yuan's son.

sentences.zh: 魏主將擊柔然，治兵於南郊，先祭天，然後部勒行陳。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor was about to attack Rouran; he drilled troops at the southern suburb, sacrificed to Heaven first, then arrayed the marching formations.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor prepared to attack Rouran; he drilled troops at the southern suburb, sacrificed to Heaven, then drew up battle lines.

sentences.zh: 內外群臣皆不欲行，保太后固止之，獨崔浩勸之。

translations.literal: Ministers within and without all wished not to go; Empress Dowager Bao firmly dissuaded him; only Cui Hao urged the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Court and camp alike opposed the campaign; Empress Dowager Bao firmly dissuaded him; only Cui Hao urged him on.

sentences.zh: 尚書令劉絜等共推太史令張淵、徐辯使言於魏主曰：「今茲己巳，三陰之歲，歲星襲月，太白在西方，不可舉兵，北伐必敗。

translations.literal: Liu Jie, Minister of State, and others jointly put forward the Grand Astrologer Zhang Yuan and Xu Bian to tell the Wei emperor: "This year is jisi, a year of triple yin; the Year Star assails the Moon and the White Star is in the west—arms must not be raised; a northern campaign will surely fail.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Liu Jie and others had the grand astrologers Zhang Yuan and Xu Bian tell the emperor: "This jisi year is dominated by yin; Jupiter assails the moon and Venus stands in the west—do not march north or you will be defeated.

sentences.zh: 雖克，不利於上。」

translations.literal: Even if victorious, it will not benefit Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Even victory would not favor Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 群臣因共贊之曰：「淵等少時嘗諫苻堅南伐，堅不從而敗，所言無不中，不可違也。」

translations.literal: The ministers thereupon all endorsed them, saying: "Yuan and the others once in their youth admonished Fu Jian against a southern campaign; Jian did not listen and was defeated—their words have never missed; they must not be disobeyed."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers chimed in: "Yuan and his colleagues once warned Fu Jian against invading the south; Jian ignored them and was ruined—their predictions never miss; you must heed them."

sentences.zh: 魏主意不決，詔浩與淵等論難於前。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor's mind was unsettled; he ordered Hao to debate Yuan and the others before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated and ordered Hao to debate Yuan and the others in court.

sentences.zh: 浩詰淵、辯曰：「陽為德，陰為刑，故日食修德，月食修刑。

translations.literal: Hao questioned Yuan and Bian, saying: "Yang is virtue and yin is punishment; therefore at a solar eclipse one cultivates virtue, and at a lunar eclipse one cultivates punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Hao challenged Yuan and Bian: "Yang is virtue and yin is punishment; a solar eclipse calls for virtue, a lunar eclipse for punishment.

sentences.zh: 夫王者用刑，小則肆諸市朝，大則陳諸原野。

translations.literal: When a king employs punishment, on a small scale it is displayed in market and court, on a large scale arrayed in the open field.
translations.idiomatic: A king's punishments, small ones are displayed in market and court; great ones are arrayed on the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 今出兵以討有罪，乃所以修刑也。

translations.literal: Now to take the field and punish the guilty is precisely how one cultivates punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Marching now to punish the guilty is precisely how we cultivate punishment.

sentences.zh: 臣竊觀天文，比年以來，月行掩昴，至今猶然。

translations.literal: Your servant has privately observed the heavens: in recent years the moon's course has veiled the Pleiades, and it is still so.
translations.idiomatic: I have watched the heavens: for years the moon has veiled the Pleiades, and it still does.

sentences.zh: 其占，三年天子大破旄頭之國。

translations.literal: The omen reads: within three years the Son of Heaven will greatly defeat the land of the Maotou.
translations.idiomatic: The omen says that within three years the Son of Heaven will crush the Maotou peoples.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕、高車，旄頭之眾也。

translations.literal: Rouran and Gaoche are peoples of the Maotou.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran and Gaoche are Maotou peoples.

sentences.zh: 願陛下勿疑。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty not to doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must not hesitate."

sentences.zh: 淵、辯復曰：「蠕蠕，荒外無用之物，得其地不可耕而食，得其民不可臣而使，輕疾無常，難得而制；

translations.literal: Yuan and Bian replied: "Rouran are useless things beyond the wilds; gain their land and you cannot farm it to eat, gain their people and you cannot make them subjects and use them; they are swift and inconstant and hard to control;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and Bian replied: "Rouran are worthless barbarians beyond the pale; their land cannot be farmed, their people cannot be ruled; they are swift, fickle, and impossible to control;

sentences.zh: 有何汲汲，而勞士馬以伐之？」

translations.literal: why be in such haste and weary soldiers and horses to attack them?"
translations.idiomatic: why weary soldiers and horses in haste to attack them?"

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「淵、辯言天道，猶是其職，至於人事形勢，尤非其所知。

translations.literal: Hao said: "Yuan and Bian speak of Heaven's Way—that is still their office; as for human affairs and strategic situation, that especially is not what they know.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said: "Yuan and Bian may speak of Heaven—that is their trade; human affairs and strategy are beyond them.

sentences.zh: 此乃漢世常談，施之於今，殊不合事宜。

translations.literal: This is the common talk of Han times; applied to today it is wholly unsuited to the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: That is Han-dynasty platitude, wholly unsuited to our day.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕本國家北邊之臣，中間叛去。

translations.literal: Rouran were originally subjects on our state's northern border and in the meantime rebelled and left.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran were once our northern subjects and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 今誅其元惡，收其良民，令復舊役，非無用也。

translations.literal: Now if we execute their chief culprits, take their good people, and make them resume their old service, they are not useless.
translations.idiomatic: Execute their leaders, take their people back into service, and they are far from useless.

sentences.zh: 世人皆謂淵、辯通解數術，明決成敗，臣請試問之：屬者統萬未亡之前，有無敗征？

translations.literal: The world all says Yuan and Bian understand numbers and fate and clearly decide success and failure—I ask to test them: before Tongwan perished recently, was there any sign of defeat?
translations.idiomatic: Everyone says Yuan and Bian read the stars and foresee outcomes—let me test them: before Tongwan fell, did they foresee defeat?

sentences.zh: 若其不知，是無術也；

translations.literal: If they did not know, they have no art;
translations.idiomatic: If they did not, they have no skill;

sentences.zh: 知而不言，是不忠也。」

translations.literal: if they knew and did not speak, that is disloyalty."
translations.idiomatic: if they knew and said nothing, that is disloyalty."

sentences.zh: 時赫連昌在坐，淵等自以未嘗有言，慚不能對。

translations.literal: At this time Helian Chang was present; Yuan and the others, knowing they had never spoken, were ashamed and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Chang was present; Yuan and his colleagues, knowing they had never warned anyone, sat ashamed and silent.

sentences.zh: 魏主大悅。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 既罷，公卿或尤浩曰：「今南寇方伺國隙，而捨之北伐；

translations.literal: When the session ended, some among the dukes and ministers reproached Hao, saying: "Now the southern enemy is watching for a gap in the state and you abandon that to campaign north;
translations.idiomatic: Afterward some ministers reproached Hao: "The southern enemy watches for our weakness, yet you abandon him to march north;

sentences.zh: 若蠕蠕遠遁，前無所獲，後有強寇，將何以待之？」

translations.literal: if Rouran flee far away and we gain nothing ahead while a strong foe is behind, how will we deal with it?"
translations.idiomatic: if Rouran flee and we gain nothing while a strong foe is behind us, what then?"

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Hao said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said: "Not so.

sentences.zh: 今不先破蠕蠕，則無以待南寇。

translations.literal: If we do not first break Rouran, we will have no means to face the southern enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Unless we break Rouran first, we cannot face the south.

sentences.zh: 南人聞國家克統萬以來，內懷恐懼，故揚聲動眾以衛淮北。

translations.literal: Since the southern people heard that the state had taken Tongwan they have harbored fear within, and therefore make a show of moving troops to guard Huaibei.
translations.idiomatic: Since we took Tongwan the southerners have been afraid; their troop movements on the Huai are bluster to guard Huaibei.

sentences.zh: 比吾破蠕蠕，往還之間，南寇必不動也。

translations.literal: By the time we break Rouran and go back and forth, the southern enemy certainly will not move.
translations.idiomatic: By the time we crush Rouran and return, the south will not stir.

sentences.zh: 且彼步我騎，彼能北來，我亦南往；

translations.literal: Moreover they are infantry and we are cavalry; they can come north and we can also go south;
translations.idiomatic: They are foot soldiers and we are horse; they can march north and we can ride south;

sentences.zh: 在彼甚困，於我未勞。

translations.literal: for them it is very taxing, for us not laborious.
translations.idiomatic: the hardship falls on them, not on us.

sentences.zh: 況南北殊俗，水陸異宜，設使國家與之河南，彼亦不能守也。

translations.literal: Moreover north and south have different customs and water and land have different advantages; even if the state gave them the lands south of the river, they could not hold them.
translations.idiomatic: North and south differ in custom and terrain; even if we gave them the lands south of the Yellow River, they could not hold them.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: How do I say this?
translations.idiomatic: How do I know?

sentences.zh: 以劉裕之雄傑，吞併關中，留其愛子，輔以良將，精兵數萬，猶不能守。

translations.literal: Liu Yu was a hero who swallowed Guanzhong, left his beloved son there assisted by good generals with tens of thousands of elite troops, yet still could not hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu was a hero who seized Guanzhong, left his beloved son there with fine generals and tens of thousands of elite troops, and still could not hold it.

sentences.zh: 全軍覆沒，號哭之聲，至今未已。

translations.literal: The whole army was destroyed; the sound of wailing has not ceased to this day.
translations.idiomatic: The army was wiped out; their wailing has not ended to this day.

sentences.zh: 況義隆今日君臣非裕時之比！

translations.literal: How much less can Yilong's ruler and ministers today compare with Liu Yu's day!
translations.idiomatic: How much less do Yilong and his court compare with Liu Yu's day!

sentences.zh: 主上英武，士馬精強，彼若果來，譬如以駒犢斗虎狼也，何懼之有！

translations.literal: Our lord is heroic and martial, soldiers and horses elite and strong; if they truly come, it will be like pitting foals and calves against tigers and wolves—what is there to fear!
translations.idiomatic: Our lord is heroic and our troops are elite; if they come, it will be foals against tigers—what is there to fear!

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕恃其絕遠，謂國家力不能制，自寬日久，故夏則散眾放畜，秋肥乃聚，背寒向溫，南來寇鈔。

translations.literal: Rouran rely on their extreme distance, thinking the state lacks strength to control them; they have long been at ease, and therefore in summer disperse their hosts to pasture livestock, gather only when fat in autumn, turn their backs on cold and face warmth, and come south to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran trust their remoteness and think we cannot reach them; they have grown complacent, scattering in summer to pasture, gathering only when the herds are fat in autumn, and raiding southward away from the cold.

sentences.zh: 今掩其不備，必望塵駭散。

translations.literal: Now if we strike them unprepared, they will surely flee in panic at the sight of dust.
translations.idiomatic: Strike them unprepared and they will flee at the first dust cloud.

sentences.zh: 牡馬護牝，牝馬戀駒，驅馳難制，不得水草，不過數日，必聚而困弊，可一舉而滅也。

translations.literal: Stallions guard mares, mares cling to foals; driven hard they are hard to control; without water and fodder, within a few days they must mass together in exhaustion and weakness and can be destroyed in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Stallions guard mares and mares cling to foals; driven hard they are unmanageable; without water and grass, within days they mass together exhausted—and we can destroy them at one blow.

sentences.zh: 暫勞永逸，時不可失，患在上無此意。

translations.literal: Brief toil for lasting ease; the moment must not be lost—the trouble was that the throne lacked this resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Brief exertion now for lasting ease; the moment must not be lost—the only problem was that the throne had not seen it that way.

sentences.zh: 今上意已決，奈何止之！」

translations.literal: Now the ruler's mind is already decided—how can you stop it!"
translations.idiomatic: The throne's mind is made up—how can you hold him back!"

sentences.zh: 寇謙之謂浩曰：「蠕蠕果可克乎？」

translations.literal: Kou Qianzhi said to Hao: "Can Rouran truly be conquered?"
translations.idiomatic: Kou Qianzhi asked Hao: "Can Rouran truly be beaten?"

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「必克。

translations.literal: Hao said: "They will surely be conquered.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said: "They can be beaten.

sentences.zh: 但恐諸將瑣瑣，前後顧慮，不能乘勝深入，使不全舉耳。」

translations.literal: I only fear the generals are petty-minded, looking before and behind with anxiety, unable to follow victory deep in pursuit, so that the whole enterprise is not completed."
translations.idiomatic: I only fear the generals are too cautious, looking over their shoulders, unable to drive the victory home and finish the job."

sentences.zh: 先是，帝因魏使者還，告魏主曰：「汝趣歸我河南地！

translations.literal: Before this, as a Wei envoy was leaving, the emperor told Wei's ruler: "Hurry and return our lands south of the Yellow River to us!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as a Wei envoy was departing, the emperor told Wei's ruler: "Return our lands south of the Yellow River at once!

sentences.zh: 不然，將盡我將士之力。」

translations.literal: Otherwise I will exhaust the strength of my officers and soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I will send every soldier I have against you."

sentences.zh: 魏主方議伐柔然，聞之大笑，謂公卿曰：「龜鱉小豎，自救不暇，夫何能為！

translations.literal: Wei's ruler was just discussing campaigning against Rouran; hearing this he laughed greatly and said to the dukes and ministers: "That turtle of a stripling can barely save himself—what can he do!
translations.idiomatic: Wei's ruler was already debating war on Rouran; hearing this he laughed and told his ministers: "That turtle of a boy can barely save himself—what could he possibly do!

sentences.zh: 就使能來，若不先滅蠕蠕，乃是坐待寇至，腹背受敵，非良策也。

translations.literal: Even if he could come, if we do not first destroy Rouran, that would be sitting and waiting for the enemy to arrive, attacked front and rear—that is no good plan.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he could march, failing to destroy Rouran first would mean sitting still while enemies hit us from both sides—no good strategy.

sentences.zh: 吾行決矣。」

translations.literal: My course is decided."
translations.idiomatic: My decision stands."

sentences.zh: 庚寅，魏主發平城，使北平王長孫嵩、廣陵公樓伏連居守。

translations.literal: On gengyin Wei's ruler set out from Pingcheng, leaving Prince of Beiping Changgunsun Song and Duke of Guangling Lou Fulian to garrison and hold the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Wei's ruler marched from Pingcheng, leaving Prince of Beiping Changgunsun Song and Duke of Guangling Lou Fulian to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 魏主自東道向黑山，使平陽王長孫翰自西道向大娥山，同會柔然之庭。

translations.literal: Wei's ruler himself took the eastern route toward Heishan, sending Prince of Pingyang Changgunsun Han by the western route toward Da'e Mountain, to meet together at Rouran's court.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's ruler took the eastern route toward Heishan while Prince of Pingyang Changgunsun Han marched west toward Da'e Mountain; both were to converge on Rouran's domain.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬辰朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day renchen, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the first day renchen, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 王敬弘固讓尚書令，表求還東。

translations.literal: Wang Jinghong firmly declined the post of Director of the Masters of Writing and memorialized asking to return east.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jinghong firmly declined Director of the Masters of Writing and petitioned to return east.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，更以敬弘為侍中、特進、左光祿大夫，聽其東歸。

translations.literal: On guisi he was again made Palace Attendant, Special Court Advancement, and Left Grandee of Splendid Happiness, and permitted to return east.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi he was made Palace Attendant, Special Court Advancement, and Left Grandee of Splendid Happiness, and allowed to go home east.

sentences.zh: 丁未，魏主至漠南，捨輜重，帥輕騎兼馬襲擊柔然，至栗水，柔然紇升蓋可汗先不設備，民畜滿野，驚怖散去，莫相收攝。

translations.literal: On dingwei Wei's ruler reached south of the desert, cast off baggage trains, and led light cavalry with double mounts in a surprise attack on Rouran; reaching Lishui, Rouran's Khan Yujiengai had not prepared defenses beforehand; people and livestock filled the fields; in terror they scattered and fled, none gathering one another.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Wei's ruler reached the southern desert, shed his baggage train, and led mounted light cavalry in a surprise raid on Rouran. At the Li River, Khan Yujiengai of Rouran was caught unprepared; people and herds filled the plains and fled in panic with no one able to regroup them.

sentences.zh: 紇升蓋燒廬舍，絕跡西走，莫知所之。

translations.literal: Yujiengai burned his yurts, cut off his trail, and fled west; none knew where he had gone.
translations.idiomatic: Yujiengai burned his camps and vanished westward; no one knew where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 其弟匹黎先主東部，聞有魏寇，帥眾欲就其兄；

translations.literal: His younger brother Piliji, who ruled the eastern branch, heard there was a Wei raid and led his host to join his elder brother;
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Piliji, who held the eastern tribes, heard of the Wei raid and marched to join his brother;

sentences.zh: 遇長孫翰，翰邀擊，大破之，殺其大人數百。

translations.literal: he met Changgunsun Han; Han intercepted and struck, routing them greatly and killing several hundred of their leaders.
translations.idiomatic: he ran into Changgunsun Han, who intercepted and crushed him, killing several hundred tribal chiefs.

sentences.zh: 夏主欲復取統萬，引兵東至侯尼城，不敢進而還。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler wished to retake Tongwan, led troops east to Houni City, dared not advance, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler tried to retake Tongwan, marched east to Houni City, lost his nerve, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜伐秦，秦王暮末留相國元基守枹罕，遷保定連。

translations.literal: King Mengsun of Hexi attacked Qin; King Mumu of Qin left the chief minister Yuanji to hold Fuhan and moved to Baodinglian.
translations.idiomatic: King Mengsun of Hexi attacked Qin; King Mumu of Qin left Chief Minister Yuanji to hold Fuhan and withdrew to Baodinglian.

sentences.zh: 南安太守翟承伯等據罕幵谷以應河西，幕末擊破之，進至治城。

translations.literal: Nan'an prefect Zhai Chengbo and others held Hanjiang Valley in response to Hexi; Mumu defeated them and advanced to Zhicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Nan'an Prefect Zhai Chengbo and others seized Hanjiang Valley to aid Hexi; Mumu routed them and pushed on to Zhicheng.

sentences.zh: 西安太守莫者幼眷據汧川以叛，暮末討之，為幼眷所敗，還於定連。

translations.literal: Xi'an prefect Mozhe Youjuan held Qianchuan in rebellion; Mumu campaigned against him, was defeated by Youjuan, and returned to Dinglian.
translations.idiomatic: Xi'an Prefect Mozhe Youjuan rebelled and held Qianchuan; Mumu attacked, was beaten by Youjuan, and fell back to Dinglian.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜至枹罕，遣世子興國進攻定連。

translations.literal: Mengsun reached Fuhan and sent his heir Xingguo to attack Dinglian.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun reached Fuhan and sent his heir Xingguo against Dinglian.

sentences.zh: 六月，暮末逆擊興國於治城，擒之，追擊蒙遜至譚郊。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Mumu met Xingguo at Zhicheng in counterattack, captured him, and pursued Mengsun to Tanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Mumu counterattacked Xingguo at Zhicheng, took him prisoner, and chased Mengsun to Tanjiao.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾王慕瑰遣其弟沒利延，將騎五千會蒙遜伐秦，暮末遣輔國大將軍段暉等邀擊，大破之。

translations.literal: King Mugui of Tuyuhun sent his younger brother Moliyan with five thousand horse to join Mengsun in attacking Qin; Mumu sent General Who Assists the State Duan Hui and others to intercept and strike, routing them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: King Mugui of Tuyuhun sent his brother Moliyan with five thousand cavalry to join Mengsun against Qin; Mumu sent General Who Assists the State Duan Hui to intercept and rout them.

sentences.zh: 柔然紇升蓋可汗既走，部落四散，竄伏山谷，雜畜布野，無人收視。

translations.literal: After Rouran Khan Yujiengai had fled, tribes scattered in all directions, hiding in valleys; mixed livestock lay across the fields with no one to gather them.
translations.idiomatic: After Khan Yujiengai of Rouran fled, the tribes scattered into the hills; livestock lay everywhere untended.

sentences.zh: 魏主循栗水西行，至菟園水，分軍搜討，東西五千里，南北三千里，俘斬甚眾。

translations.literal: Wei's ruler followed the Li River west to Tuyuan River, divided the army to search and suppress over five thousand li east to west and three thousand li north to south, capturing and killing a great multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's ruler marched west along the Li River to the Tuyuan River and sent detachments to sweep an area five thousand li east to west and three thousand li north to south, capturing and killing vast numbers.

sentences.zh: 高車諸部乘魏兵勢，鈔掠柔然。

translations.literal: The various Gaoche tribes took advantage of Wei's military momentum to raid and plunder Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoche tribes joined the Wei advance and plundered Rouran.

sentences.zh: 柔然種類前後降魏者三十餘萬落，獲戎馬百餘萬匹，畜產、車廬，瀰漫山澤，亡慮數百萬。

translations.literal: Rouran tribes who submitted to Wei before and after totaled more than three hundred thousand households; they captured more than a million war horses; livestock, carts, and tents flooded the mountains and marshes—in incalculable millions.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred thousand Rouran households surrendered to Wei; they seized over a million war horses, and livestock, carts, and tents covered the hills and marshes—in the millions beyond count.

sentences.zh: 魏主循弱水西行，至涿邪山，諸將慮深入有伏兵，勸魏主留止，寇謙之以崔浩之言告魏主，魏主不從。

translations.literal: Wei's ruler followed the Ruoshui west to Zhuoye Mountain; the generals feared going deep and hitting an ambush and urged Wei's ruler to halt; Kou Qianzhi told Wei's ruler Cui Hao's words, but Wei's ruler would not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's ruler marched west along the Ruoshui to Zhuoye Mountain; the generals feared ambush in the deep country and urged him to stop; Kou Qianzhi relayed Cui Hao's counsel, but Wei's ruler refused.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，引兵東還；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, he led the army east and returned;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he turned east and marched home;

sentences.zh: 至黑山，以所獲班賜將士有差。

translations.literal: reaching Heishan, he distributed the spoils among officers and soldiers in varying measures.
translations.idiomatic: at Heishan he distributed the spoils among the troops by rank.

sentences.zh: 既而得降人言：「可汗先被病，聞魏兵至，不知所為，乃焚穹廬，以車自載，將數百人入南山。

translations.literal: Then they got word from captives: "The khan had been ill beforehand; hearing Wei troops had come, he did not know what to do, so he burned his felt tents, loaded himself onto carts, and with several hundred men entered the southern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Captives then reported: "The khan had already been ill; when he heard Wei troops were coming he did not know what to do, burned his tents, loaded carts, and with a few hundred men entered the southern mountains.

sentences.zh: 民畜窘聚，方六十里無人統領，相去百八十里，追兵不至，乃徐西遁，唯此得免。」

translations.literal: People and livestock were jammed together over a square of sixty li with no one in command; separated by one hundred eighty li, pursuers did not reach them, and only then did they slowly flee west and escape."
translations.idiomatic: People and herds were packed within a sixty-li square with no leader; a hundred eighty li ahead of the pursuit, they slipped slowly west—the only way he escaped."

sentences.zh: 後聞涼州賈胡言：「若復前行二日，則盡滅之矣。」

translations.literal: Later they heard from a Liangzhou merchant: "If we had marched two more days, we would have wiped them out completely."
translations.idiomatic: Later a Liangzhou trader said: "Two more days' march would have destroyed them entirely."

sentences.zh: 魏主深悔之。

translations.literal: Wei's ruler deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's ruler deeply regretted it.

sentences.zh: 紇升蓋可汗憤悒而卒，子吳提立，號敕連可汗。

translations.literal: Khan Yujiengai died of vexation and distress; his son Wuti succeeded him, taking the title Khan Chelian.
translations.idiomatic: Khan Yujiengai died of grief; his son Wuti succeeded him as Khan Chelian.

sentences.zh: 武都孝昭王楊玄疾病，欲以國授其弟難當。

translations.literal: Yang Xuan, Filial and Bright King of Wudu, was ill and wished to give the state to his younger brother Nandang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuan, Filial and Bright King of Wudu, fell ill and wanted to pass the realm to his brother Nandang.

sentences.zh: 難當固辭，請立玄子保宗而輔之；

translations.literal: Nandang firmly declined and asked that Xuan's son Baozong be established while he assisted him;
translations.idiomatic: Nandang refused and asked that Xuan's son Baozong be enthroned while he served as regent;

sentences.zh: 玄許之。

translations.literal: Xuan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan agreed.

sentences.zh: 玄卒，保宗立。

translations.literal: Xuan died and Baozong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan died and Baozong took the throne.

sentences.zh: 難當妻姚氏勸難當自立，難當乃廢保宗，自稱都督雍、涼、秦三州諸軍事、征西大將軍、開府儀同三司、秦州刺史、武都王。

translations.literal: Nandang's wife Lady Yao urged Nandang to take power himself; Nandang then deposed Baozong and styled himself Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in Yong, Liang, and Qin Provinces, General Who Conquers the West, Grand General with Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies, Governor of Qin Province, and King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang's wife Lady Yao urged him to seize power; he deposed Baozong and declared himself Commander-in-Chief of Yong, Liang, and Qin, General Who Conquers the West, Grand General with Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies, Governor of Qin Province, and King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜遣使送谷三十萬斛以贖世子興國於秦，秦王暮末不許。

translations.literal: King Mengsun of Hexi sent envoys with three hundred thousand hu of grain to ransom his heir Xingguo from Qin; King Mumu of Qin would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: King Mengsun of Hexi sent grain—three hundred thousand hu—to ransom his heir Xingguo from Qin; King Mumu refused.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜乃立興國母弟菩提為世子。

translations.literal: Mengsun then established Xingguo's younger brother by the same mother, Puti, as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun then named Xingguo's younger full brother Puti as heir.

sentences.zh: 暮末以興國為散騎常侍，以其妹平昌公主妻之。

translations.literal: Mumu made Xingguo Attendant Cavalier at Large and gave him his younger sister, the Princess of Pingchang, in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Mumu made Xingguo Attendant Cavalier at Large and married him to his sister, Princess of Pingchang.

sentences.zh: 八月，魏主至漠南，聞高車東部屯巳尼陂，人畜甚眾，去魏軍千餘里，遣左僕射安原等將萬騎擊之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Wei's ruler reached south of the desert, heard the eastern Gaoche were encamped at Sinipo with very many people and livestock, more than a thousand li from Wei's army, and sent Left Deputy Director Anyuan and others with ten thousand horse to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Wei's ruler reached the southern desert, learned the eastern Gaoche were camped at Sinipo with vast herds a thousand li away, and sent Left Deputy Director Anyuan with ten thousand horse against them.

sentences.zh: 高車諸部迎降者數十萬落，獲馬牛羊百餘萬。

translations.literal: Gaoche tribes who came forward to surrender numbered several hundred thousand households; they captured more than a million horses, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred thousand Gaoche households surrendered; they seized more than a million horses, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Wei's ruler returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Wei's ruler returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 徙柔然、高車降附之民於漠南，東至濡源，西暨五原陰山，三千里中，使之耕牧而收其貢賦；

translations.literal: He moved Rouran and Gaoche people who had submitted and attached themselves to south of the desert, from east at Ruyuan to west reaching Wuyuan and the Yin Mountains, within three thousand li, making them farm and pasture while collecting their tribute and levies;
translations.idiomatic: He resettled submitted Rouran and Gaoche on the southern desert from Ruyuan in the east to Wuyuan and the Yin Mountains in the west—three thousand li—set them to farming and herding, and collected tribute;

sentences.zh: 命長孫翰、劉絜、安原及侍中代人古弼同鎮撫之。

translations.literal: he ordered Changgunsun Han, Liu Jie, Anyuan, and Palace Attendant and tribal submitter Gu Bi jointly to garrison and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: he put Changgunsun Han, Liu Jie, Anyuan, and Palace Attendant Gu Bi, a tribesman who had submitted, in joint charge of pacifying them.

sentences.zh: 自是魏之民間馬牛羊及氈皮為之價賤。

translations.literal: From this the prices of horses, cattle, sheep, and felt skins among Wei's common people fell.
translations.idiomatic: From then on horses, cattle, sheep, and felt skins were cheap throughout Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏主加崔浩侍中、特進、撫軍大將軍，以賞其謀畫之功。

translations.literal: Wei's ruler promoted Cui Hao to Palace Attendant, Special Court Advancement, and General Who Pacifies the Army, to reward his merit in planning and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's ruler promoted Cui Hao to Palace Attendant, Special Court Advancement, and General Who Pacifies the Army, rewarding his strategic counsel.

sentences.zh: 浩善占天文，常置銅鋌於酢器中，夜有所見，即以鋌畫紙作字以記其異。

translations.literal: Hao was skilled at reading the heavens; he often placed a copper awl in a vinegar jar, and when he saw something at night he would use the awl to trace characters on paper to record the anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was skilled at reading the heavens; he kept a copper stylus in a vinegar jar, and when he saw something in the night sky he scratched characters on paper to record the omen.

sentences.zh: 魏主每如浩家，問以災異，或倉猝不及束帶；

translations.literal: Wei's ruler often went to Hao's home to ask about disasters and anomalies; sometimes in haste Hao could not finish tying his sash;
translations.idiomatic: Wei's ruler often visited Hao to ask about omens; sometimes Hao had no time even to belt his robe;

sentences.zh: 奉進疏食，不暇精美，魏主必為之舉箸，或立嘗而還。

translations.literal: he would serve plain food without time to make it fine; Wei's ruler always picked up chopsticks for it, sometimes tasting while standing and then leaving.
translations.idiomatic: he served plain food in haste; Wei's ruler always ate with him—sometimes standing for a bite before leaving.

sentences.zh: 魏主嘗引浩出入臥內，從容謂浩曰：「卿才智淵博，事朕祖考，著忠三世，故朕引卿以自近。

translations.literal: Wei's ruler once had Hao enter and leave his sleeping quarters and said at ease to Hao: "Your talent and learning are profound and broad; you served my forefathers and have shown loyalty through three reigns, so I keep you close.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's ruler once brought Hao in and out of his private chambers and said gently: "Your learning runs deep; you served my forefathers with loyalty through three reigns, and that is why I keep you near.

sentences.zh: 卿宜盡忠規諫，勿有所隱。

translations.literal: You should exhaust loyalty in remonstrance and counsel—hide nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Speak your mind fully in counsel—hide nothing from me.

sentences.zh: 朕雖或時忿恚，不從卿言，然終久深思卿言也。」

translations.literal: Although I may at times grow angry and not follow your words, in the end I always ponder your words deeply."
translations.idiomatic: I may grow angry and refuse you in the moment, but in the end I always weigh what you say."

sentences.zh: 嘗指浩以示新降高車渠帥曰：「汝曹視此人尪纖懦弱，不能彎弓持矛，然其胸中所懷，乃過於兵甲。

translations.literal: He once pointed to Hao to show newly submitted Gaoche chieftains and said: "You people see this man—frail, thin, and weak, unable to bend a bow or hold a spear—yet what he carries in his breast surpasses armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Once he pointed Hao out to newly submitted Gaoche chiefs and said: "You see this man—frail and weak, unable to bend a bow—yet what he carries inside is worth more than armor.

sentences.zh: 朕雖有征伐之志而不能自決，前後有功，皆此人所教也。」
