translations.literal: Although I have the will to campaign I cannot decide for myself; successes before and after have all been taught by this man."
translations.idiomatic: I mean to conquer but cannot decide alone; every victory has come from this man's counsel."

sentences.zh: 又敕尚書曰：「凡軍國大計，汝曹所不能決者，皆當咨浩，然後施行。」

translations.literal: He also instructed the Masters of Writing: "On all major plans of army and state that you cannot decide, you must consult Hao before carrying them out."
translations.idiomatic: He also told the Masters of Writing: "On any major plan of war or state you cannot settle, consult Hao before acting."

sentences.zh: 秦王暮末之弟軻殊羅烝於文昭王左夫人禿髮氏，暮末知而禁之。

translations.literal: King Mumu of Qin's younger brother Kesheluo carried on with Lady Tufa, left consort of King Wenzhao; Mumu learned of it and forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: King Mumu of Qin's brother Kesheluo took up with Lady Tufa, left consort of King Wenzhao; Mumu found out and forbade it.

sentences.zh: 軻殊羅懼，與叔父什寅謀殺暮末，奉沮渠興國以奔河西。

translations.literal: Kesheluo was afraid and with his uncle Shiyin plotted to kill Mumu, install Juqu Xingguo, and flee to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Kesheluo, afraid, joined his uncle Shiyin in a plot to kill Mumu, put Juqu Xingguo on the throne, and flee to Hexi.

sentences.zh: 使禿髮氏盜門鑰，鑰誤，門者以告暮末。

translations.literal: They had Lady Tufa steal the gate keys; the keys were wrong, and the gatekeeper reported to Mumu.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Lady Tufa to steal the gate keys; she took the wrong ones, and the gatekeeper told Mumu.

sentences.zh: 暮末悉收其黨殺之，而赦軻殊羅。

translations.literal: Mumu arrested all their faction and killed them, but pardoned Kesheluo.
translations.idiomatic: Mumu arrested the plotters and executed them, but spared Kesheluo.

sentences.zh: 執什寅，鞭之，什寅曰：「我負汝死，不負汝鞭！」

translations.literal: He seized Shiyin and whipped him; Shiyin said: "I owe you death—I do not owe you the whip!"
translations.idiomatic: He seized Shiyin and had him flogged; Shiyin said: "I owe you my death—I do not owe you this beating!"

sentences.zh: 暮末怒，刳其腹，投屍於河。

translations.literal: Mumu was enraged, disemboweled him, and threw his corpse into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Mumu cut open his belly and threw the body into the river.

sentences.zh: 夏主少凶暴無賴，不為世祖所知。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler from youth was fierce, violent, and worthless, and was not understood by Emperor Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: From youth the Xia ruler had been violent and unrestrained, misunderstood by Emperor Shizu.

sentences.zh: 是月，畋於陰槃，登苛藍山，望統城泣曰：「先帝若以朕承大業者，豈有今日之事乎！」

translations.literal: That month, hunting at Yinpan, he climbed Mount Kelan, looked toward Tongcheng, and wept, saying: "If the late emperor had meant me to inherit the great enterprise, how could there be today's affair!"
translations.idiomatic: That month, hunting at Yinpan, he climbed Mount Kelan, gazed toward Tongcheng, and wept: "If my father had meant me to inherit the throne, would things be as they are today!"

sentences.zh: 十一月，己丑朔，日有食之，不盡如鉤，星晝見，至晡方沒，河北地暗。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day jichou, there was an eclipse of the sun incomplete like a hook; stars were visible by day until dusk before they set; the land north of the river was dark.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the first day jichou, the sun was eclipsed to a hook; stars shone by day until dusk; north of the river went dark.

sentences.zh: 魏主西巡，至柞山。

translations.literal: Wei's ruler toured west and reached Zuoshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's ruler toured west to Zuoshan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，河西王蒙遜、吐谷渾王慕瑰皆遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month King Mengsun of Hexi and King Mugui of Tuyuhun both sent envoys to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Kings Mengsun of Hexi and Mugui of Tuyuhun both sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏內都大官中山文懿公李先、青冀二州刺史安同皆卒。

translations.literal: That year Li Xian, Grand Provisioner of the Inner Capital of Wei and Duke Wenyi of Zhongshan, and Ang Tong, governor of Qing and Ji Provinces, both died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Xian, Wei's Grand Provisioner and Duke Wenyi of Zhongshan, and Ang Tong, governor of Qing and Ji, both died.

sentences.zh: 先年九十五。

translations.literal: Xian was ninety-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was ninety-five.

sentences.zh: 秦地震，野草皆自反。

translations.literal: Qin had an earthquake; wild grass all turned itself over.
translations.idiomatic: Qin was shaken by an earthquake; wild grass turned upside down.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝上之中元嘉七年（

translations.literal: The seventh year of Yuanjia, middle period of the first reign of Emperor Wen of Song (
translations.idiomatic: Seventh year of Yuanjia under the first reign of Emperor Wen of Song (

sentences.zh: 庚午，公元四三零年）

translations.literal: gengwu, the year 430 CE)
translations.idiomatic: the year gengwu, 430 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸巳，以吐谷渾王慕瑰為征西將軍，沙州刺史、隴西公。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guisi, King Mugui of Tuyuhun was made General Who Conquers the West, Governor of Shazhou, and Duke of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guisi, King Mugui of Tuyuhun was made General Who Conquers the West, Governor of Shazhou, and Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 庚子，魏主還宮。

translations.literal: On gengzi Wei's ruler returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Wei's ruler returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，大赦。

translations.literal: On renyin there was a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin he declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 癸卿，復如廣寧，臨溫泉。

translations.literal: On guimao he again went to Guangning to visit the hot springs.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao he again went to Guangning to visit the hot springs.

sentences.zh: 二月，西卿，魏平陽威王長孫翰卒。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinmao, Prince Wei of Pingyang Changgunsun Han died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinmao, Prince Wei of Pingyang Changgunsun Han died.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，魏主還宮。

translations.literal: On wuchen Wei's ruler returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Wei's ruler returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝自踐位以來，有恢復河南之志。

translations.literal: Since the emperor acceded to the throne he has had the will to recover the lands south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Since his accession the emperor had wanted to recover the lands south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊子詔簡甲卒五萬給右將軍到彥之，統安北將軍王仲德、袞州刺史竺靈秀舟師入河，又使驍騎將軍段宏將精騎八千直指虎牢，豫州刺史劉德武將兵一萬繼進，後將軍長沙王義欣將兵三萬監征討諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the third month, on wuzi, he ordered fifty thousand armored soldiers selected and given to General of the Right Dao Yanzhi, who would command General Who Pacifies the North Wang Zhongde and Governor of Yanzhou Zhu Lingxiu's river fleet to enter the river; he also sent General of Valiant Cavalry Duan Hong with eight thousand elite horse straight at Hulao, Governor of Yuzhou Liu Dewu with ten thousand troops to follow, and General of the Rear the Prince of Changsha Yixin with thirty thousand troops to supervise all punitive campaign affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuzi, he drafted fifty thousand armored troops for General of the Right Dao Yanzhi, who would lead General Who Pacifies the North Wang Zhongde and Yanzhou Governor Zhu Lingxiu's fleet up the river; he sent General of Valiant Cavalry Duan Hong with eight thousand elite cavalry straight for Hulao, Yuzhou Governor Liu Dewu with ten thousand men in support, and General of the Rear Prince of Changsha Yixin with thirty thousand men to oversee the campaign.

sentences.zh: 義欣，道憐之子也。

translations.literal: Yixin was the son of Dao Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin was Dao Lin's son.

sentences.zh: 先遣殿中將軍田奇使於魏，告魏主曰：「河南舊是宋土，中為彼所侵，今當修復舊境，不關河北。」

translations.literal: First he sent Palace Army General Tian Qi as envoy to Wei, telling Wei's ruler: "The lands south of the Yellow River were formerly Song territory; in the middle they were invaded by you—now we shall restore the old borders; this does not concern the lands north of the river."
translations.idiomatic: He first sent Palace Army General Tian Qi to Wei with a message: "The lands south of the Yellow River were Song soil until you seized them; we mean only to restore the old border—not to touch the north."

sentences.zh: 魏主大怒曰：「我生發未燥，已聞河南是我地。

translations.literal: Wei's ruler was greatly enraged and said: "Before my hair was dry I already heard that the lands south of the Yellow River were my territory.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's ruler flew into a rage: "Before my hair was dry I heard those lands south of the Yellow River were mine.

sentences.zh: 此豈可得！

translations.literal: How can this be granted!
translations.idiomatic: That will never happen!

sentences.zh: 必若進軍，今當權斂戍相避，須冬寒地淨，河冰堅合，自更取之。」

translations.literal: If you must advance, for now I shall temporarily withdraw garrisons and make way; when winter cold clears the ground and river ice is firmly joined, I will take it back myself."
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on marching, I will pull back the garrisons for now—but when winter freezes the ground and the river, I will take it back myself."

sentences.zh: 甲午，以前南廣平太守尹沖為司州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiawu the former Governor of Southern Guangping Yin Chong was made Governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu former Southern Guangping Governor Yin Chong was appointed Governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 長沙王義欣出鎮彭城，為眾軍聲援。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changsha Yixin went out to garrison Pengcheng as a vocal reinforcement for the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Changsha Yixin took command at Pengcheng to support the main army.

sentences.zh: 以游擊將軍胡籓戍廣陵，行府州事。

translations.literal: General of Mobile Columns Hu Fan was stationed at Guangling to act in the affairs of the prefecture and province.
translations.idiomatic: General of Mobile Columns Hu Fan was posted at Guangling with prefectural and provincial authority.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，魏封赫連昌為秦王。

translations.literal: On renyin Wei enfeoffed Helian Chang as King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Wei enfeoffed Helian Chang as King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 魏有新徒敕勒千餘家，苦於將吏侵漁，出怨言，期以草生牛馬肥，亡歸漠北。

translations.literal: In Wei there were newly resettled Tiele families, more than a thousand households, suffering from the encroachments and extortions of officers and clerks; they voiced grievances and fixed on the time when grass would grow and oxen and horses grow fat to flee north and return to the desert north.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand newly resettled Tiele households in Wei groaned under the predations of garrison officers and officials; they whispered that once the grass grew and the livestock fattened, they would flee back to the northern steppe.

sentences.zh: 尚書令劉絜、左僕射安原奏請及河冰未解，徙之河西。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Liu Jie and Left Deputy Director An Yuan memorialized asking that, while the river ice had not yet melted, they be moved west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Liu Jie and Left Deputy Director An Yuan urged that the tribes be relocated west of the Yellow River before the ice broke.

sentences.zh: 向春冰解，使不得北遁。

translations.literal: Facing spring when the ice melted, they would be unable to flee north.
translations.idiomatic: With the thaw of spring, they would be unable to escape northward.

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「此曹習俗，放散日久，譬如囿中之鹿，急則奔突，緩之自定。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said: "These people by custom have been scattered for a long time; it is like deer in an enclosure — pressed hard they charge and break out, eased they settle of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor said, "These people have long lived scattered by custom. They are like deer in a park — drive them hard and they burst out in panic; give them ease and they settle on their own.

sentences.zh: 吾區處自有道，不煩徙也。」

translations.literal: I have my own way of managing them; there is no need to trouble with resettlement."
translations.idiomatic: I have my own way of managing them — there is no need to relocate them."

sentences.zh: 絜等固請不已，乃聽分徙三萬餘落於河西，西至白鹽池。

translations.literal: Jie and the others pressed their request without cease; he then permitted the division and resettlement of more than thirty thousand clans west of the river, westward as far as the White Salt Pool.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jie and his colleagues persisted until the emperor agreed to resettle more than thirty thousand clans west of the river, as far as the White Salt Pool.

sentences.zh: 敕勒皆驚駭，曰：「圈我於河西，欲殺我也！」

translations.literal: The Tiele were all alarmed and said: "They are penning us west of the river intending to kill us!"
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele were terrified. "They are penning us west of the river to slaughter us!"

sentences.zh: 謀西奔涼州。

translations.literal: They plotted to flee west to Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: They plotted to flee west to Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 劉絜屯五原河北，安原屯悅拔城以備之。

translations.literal: Liu Jie encamped north of the river at Wuyuan; An Yuan encamped at Yueba city to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jie encamped north of the Wuyuan stretch of the Yellow River; An Yuan took up position at Yueba to block them.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，敕勒數千騎叛，北走，絜追討之；

translations.literal: On guimao several thousand Tiele horsemen rebelled and fled north; Jie pursued and attacked them;
translations.idiomatic: On guimao several thousand Tiele horsemen rebelled and fled north; Liu Jie pursued them;

sentences.zh: 走者無食，相枕而死。

translations.literal: The fugitives had no food and died lying one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: The fugitives, starving, died in heaps atop one another.

sentences.zh: 魏南邊諸將表稱：「宋人大嚴，將入寇。

translations.literal: The generals on Wei's southern frontier submitted memorials saying: "The Liu Song are greatly preparing their forces and will invade.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's southern commanders reported: "The Liu Song are mobilizing in force and mean to invade.

sentences.zh: 請兵三萬，先其未發，逆擊之，足以挫其銳氣，使不敢深入。」

translations.literal: We request thirty thousand troops to strike them before they set out, meeting them head-on — enough to blunt their keen momentum and make them dare not penetrate deeply."
translations.idiomatic: Give us thirty thousand men to strike before they march — a preemptive blow would break their momentum and keep them from advancing far."

sentences.zh: 因請悉誅河北流民在境上者，以絕其鄉導。

translations.literal: They also asked that all refugees from north of the river on the frontier be wholly executed to cut off their guides.
translations.idiomatic: They also asked to kill every refugee from north of the river along the border, so that Liu Song would have no local guides.

sentences.zh: 魏主使公卿議之，皆以為當然。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler had the ministers discuss it; all considered it proper.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor referred the matter to his ministers; all agreed it was the right course.

sentences.zh: 崔浩曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Cui Hao said: "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao said, "No.

sentences.zh: 南方下濕，入夏之後，水潦方降，草木蒙密，地氣鬱蒸，易生疾癘，不可行師。

translations.literal: The south is low and damp; after summer begins floods descend, grasses and trees are thick, the earth's vapors steam and stagnate, sicknesses arise easily — troops cannot be marched.
translations.idiomatic: The south is low and damp; once summer comes, floods rise, the undergrowth grows dense, and the miasma breeds pestilence — no army can march there.

sentences.zh: 且彼既嚴備，則城守必固，留屯久攻，則糧運不繼；

translations.literal: Moreover if they are already on full alert, city defense will surely be firm; if we remain encamped and attack for long, grain transport will not keep up;
translations.idiomatic: And if they are already on guard, their cities will hold fast; a prolonged siege will outrun our supplies;

sentences.zh: 分軍四掠，則眾力單寡，無以應敵。

translations.literal: if we divide the army to plunder in four directions, our forces will be thin and few, with nothing wherewith to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: if we split the army to raid in every direction, our strength will be scattered and we will be unable to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 以今擊之，未見其利。

translations.literal: To strike them now — no advantage is seen.
translations.idiomatic: An attack now offers no clear gain.

sentences.zh: 彼若果能北來，宜待其勞倦，秋涼馬肥，因敵取食，徐往擊之，此萬全之計也。

translations.literal: If they can truly come north, we should wait until they are weary, when autumn is cool and horses are fat, take food from the enemy, and go slowly to strike them — this is a plan of complete security.
translations.idiomatic: If they truly march north, wait until they are exhausted — when autumn turns cool and the horses grow fat, live off the enemy's stores, and strike at leisure. That is the sure plan.

sentences.zh: 朝廷群臣及西北守將，從陛下征伐，西平赫連，北破蠕蠕，多獲美女、珍寶，牛馬成群。

translations.literal: The court ministers and the frontier commanders of the northwest, following Your Majesty on campaigns, pacified Helian in the west and broke the Rouran in the north, obtaining many beautiful women, jewels, and treasures, cattle and horses in herds.
translations.idiomatic: The court ministers and northwestern frontier commanders who followed Your Majesty west against Helian and north against the Rouran came home with captive women, jewels, and herds of horses —

sentences.zh: 南邊諸將聞而慕之，亦欲南鈔以取資財，皆營私計，為國生事，不可從也。」

translations.literal: The southern commanders heard of this and envied it; they too wish to raid south for wealth — all are pursuing private schemes and creating trouble for the state; this cannot be followed."
translations.idiomatic: the southern commanders heard these tales and wanted their own — they urge a southern raid for loot, each pursuing private gain while inviting trouble for the state. Do not heed them."

sentences.zh: 魏主乃止。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 諸將復表：「南寇已至，所部兵少，乞簡幽州以南勁兵助己戍守，乃就漳水造船嚴備以拒之。」

translations.literal: The generals again submitted memorials: "The southern invaders have already arrived; the troops under our command are few; we beg to select elite troops from south of You Province to aid us in garrison duty; then build ships on the Zhang River and prepare strictly to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: The generals petitioned again: "The southern enemy is here, and our commands are understrength. Select crack troops from south of You Province to reinforce us, build warships on the Zhang River, and stand ready to repel them."

sentences.zh: 公卿皆以為宜如所請，並署司馬楚之、魯軌、延之等為將帥，使招誘南人。

translations.literal: The ministers all considered it right to do as requested; they jointly appointed Sima Chuzhi, Lu Gui, Yan Zhi, and others as generals to recruit and entice southerners.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers agreed. Sima Chuzhi, Lu Gui, Yan Zhi, and others were appointed to command forces tasked with recruiting southerners.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「非長策也。

translations.literal: Hao said: "This is not a long-term strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao said, "That is no sound strategy.

sentences.zh: 楚之等皆彼所畏忌，今聞國家悉發幽州以南精兵，大造舟艦，隨以輕騎，謂國家欲存立司馬氏，誅除劉宗，必舉國震駭，懼於滅亡，當悉發精銳，並心竭力，以死爭之，則我南邊諸將無以御之。

translations.literal: Chuzhi and the others are all feared and hated by them; now if they hear the state is mobilizing all elite troops south of You Province, building great numbers of ships, followed by light cavalry, they will suppose the state intends to restore the Sima house and extirpate the Liu clan; they will surely be shaken throughout the realm, terrified of destruction, and will deploy all elite forces with one heart and full strength to struggle to the death — then our southern commanders will have nothing wherewith to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Chuzhi and the others are precisely the men Liu Song fear most. If they hear Wei mobilizing every crack soldier south of You Province, building a great fleet and sending light cavalry, they will believe Wei means to restore the Sima and destroy the Liu — the whole kingdom will panic, muster every blade, and fight to the death. Our southern commanders could not stand against that.

sentences.zh: 今公卿欲以威力卻敵，乃所以速之也。

translations.literal: Now the ministers wish to repel the enemy by show of force — this is precisely what will hasten them.
translations.idiomatic: Your ministers mean to frighten the enemy off with a show of force — that is exactly what will hurry them forward.

sentences.zh: 張虛聲而召實害，此之謂矣。

translations.literal: To spread an empty threat and summon real harm — this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: An empty threat that provokes real danger — that is what this would be.

sentences.zh: 故楚之之徒，往則彼來，止則彼息，其勢然也。

translations.literal: Therefore Chuzhi and his sort — if they go, the enemy comes; if they stop, the enemy rests; such is the tendency.
translations.idiomatic: With men like Sima Chuzhi, when they advance the enemy advances; when they halt, the enemy halts. That is the pattern.

sentences.zh: 且楚之等皆纖利小才，止能招合輕薄無賴而不能成大功，徒使國家兵連禍結而已。

translations.literal: Moreover Chuzhi and the others are all petty talents grasping small gain; they can only gather the frivolous and worthless and cannot achieve great success — they will only leave the state entangled in continuous war and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Sima Chuzhi and his ilk are petty schemers who can rally riffraff but cannot win great victories — they would only bind the state in endless war.

sentences.zh: 昔魯軌說姚興以取荊州，至則敗散，為蠻人掠賣為奴，終於禍及姚泓，此已然之效也。」

translations.literal: Formerly Lu Gui persuaded Yao Xing to take Jing Province; when he arrived his forces were defeated and scattered; he was seized and sold as a slave by barbarians; in the end disaster reached Yao Hong — this is an effect already seen."
translations.idiomatic: Remember Lu Gui: he persuaded Yao Xing of Later Qin to seize Jing Province, only to see his force routed and himself sold into slavery by tribesmen — disaster that ultimately consumed Yao Hong. The precedent stands."

sentences.zh: 魏主未以為然。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler did not consider it so.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor was not persuaded.

sentences.zh: 浩乃復陳天時，以為南方舉兵必不利，曰：「今茲害氣在揚州，一也；

translations.literal: Hao then again set forth the celestial signs, holding that raising troops in the south would surely be unfavorable, saying: "This year the baleful qi is in Yang Province — one;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao then cited heaven's signs, arguing that a southern campaign must fail: "This year baleful qi afflict Yang Province — the first omen;

sentences.zh: 庚午自刑，先發者傷，二也；

translations.literal: gengwu self-punishes; whoever moves first is harmed — two;
translations.idiomatic: gengwu carries self-destruction — whoever strikes first will be hurt; the second omen;

sentences.zh: 日食晝晦，宿值斗、牛，三也；

translations.literal: an eclipse darkens the day, the lodges fall in Dipper and Ox — three;
translations.idiomatic: a solar eclipse dims the daylight under the lodges of Dipper and Ox — the third;

sentences.zh: 熒惑伏於翼、軫，主亂及喪，四也；

translations.literal: Mars lies hidden in Wings and Chariot, governing disorder and mourning — four;
translations.idiomatic: Mars hides in Wings and Chariot, augury of rebellion and death — the fourth;

sentences.zh: 太白未出，進兵者敗，五也。

translations.literal: Venus has not yet risen; whoever advances troops is defeated — five.
translations.idiomatic: Venus has not yet risen — whoever advances will be defeated. That is the fifth.

sentences.zh: 夫興國之君，先修人事，次盡地利，後觀天時，故萬舉萬全。

translations.literal: A ruler who founds a state first cultivates human affairs, next exhausts earthly advantage, afterward observes celestial timing — thus every move is fully secure.
translations.idiomatic: A founding king puts human affairs first, terrain second, and heaven last — then every venture succeeds.

sentences.zh: 今劉義隆新造之國，人事未洽；

translations.literal: Now Liu Yilong's newly founded state — human affairs are not yet harmonious;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yilong's realm is newly founded and its people not yet united;

sentences.zh: 災變屢見，天時不協；

translations.literal: calamities and portents appear repeatedly, celestial timing is not in accord;
translations.idiomatic: omens multiply and heaven is not on his side;

sentences.zh: 舟行水涸，地利不盡。

translations.literal: ships sail while water dries, earthly advantage is not fully possessed.
translations.idiomatic: his fleets move while the rivers run low — the terrain offers no advantage.

sentences.zh: 三者無一可，而義隆行之，必敗無疑。」

translations.literal: Of the three not one is available, yet Yilong is acting — defeat is certain without doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Not one of the three supports him, yet Yilong presses on — defeat is certain."

sentences.zh: 魏主不能違眾言，乃詔冀、定、相三州造船三千艘，簡幽州以南戍兵集河上以備之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler could not go against the multitude's words; he then ordered the three provinces of Ji, Ding, and Xiang to build three thousand ships, selected garrison troops from south of You Province and gathered them on the river to prepare against them.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to overrule the court, the Wei emperor ordered Ji, Ding, and Xiang to build three thousand ships and mustered garrison troops from south of You Province along the river.

sentences.zh: 秦乞伏什寅母弟前將軍白養、鎮衛將軍去列，以什寅之死，有怨言，秦王暮末皆殺之。

translations.literal: In Qin, Bai Yang the former general and younger brother of the same mother as Qifu Shiyin, and Guard General Qu Lie — because of Shiyin's death they had resentful words; King Mumu of Qin executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: In Western Qin, Former General Bai Yang — Qifu Shiyin's younger maternal half-brother — and Guard General Qu Lie nursed grievances over Shiyin's death; King Mumu had them both executed.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲子，魏主如去中。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiazi, the Wei ruler went to Quzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on jiazi, the Wei emperor traveled to Quzhong.

sentences.zh: 敕勒萬餘落復叛走，魏主使尚書封鐵追討，滅之。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand Tiele clans again rebelled and fled; the Wei ruler sent Minister of Documents Feng Tie to pursue and attack; he destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand Tiele clans rebelled and fled again; the Wei emperor sent Minister of Documents Feng Tie in pursuit and annihilated them.

sentences.zh: 六月，己卿，以氐王楊難當為冠軍將軍、秦州刺史、武都王。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jimao, the Di king Yang Nandang was made General Who Establishes Martial Supremacy, Governor of Qin Province, and King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jimao, the Di king Yang Nandang was appointed General Who Establishes Martial Supremacy, Governor of Qin Province, and King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 魏主使平南大將軍、丹楊王大毘，屯河上，以司馬楚之為安南大將軍、荊州刺史，封琅邪王，頓穎川以備宋。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler sent Grand General Who Pacifies the South, Prince Danyang Da Pi, to encamp on the river; he made Sima Chuzhi General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Jing Province, enfeoffed him as King of Langye, and stationed him at Yingchuan to guard against Liu Song.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor posted Grand General Who Pacifies the South Prince Danyang Da Pi along the river; he made Sima Chuzhi General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Jing Province, enfeoffed him as King of Langye, and stationed him at Yingchuan against Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾王慕瑰將其眾萬八千襲秦定連，秦輔國大將軍段暉等擊走之。

translations.literal: King Mugui of Tuyuhun led his force of eighteen thousand to raid Dinglian in Qin; General Who Assists the State Duan Hui of Qin and others attacked and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: King Mugui of Tuyuhun led eighteen thousand men against Dinglian in Qin; Western Qin's General Who Assists the State Duan Hui beat them back.

sentences.zh: 到彥之自淮入泗，水滲，日行才十里，自四月至秋七月，始至須昌。

translations.literal: Dao Yanzhi entered the Si from the Huai; the water was low; each day he advanced only ten li; from the fourth month until the seventh month of autumn he finally reached Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Yanzhi entered the Si from the Huai, but the water was so shallow his fleet managed only ten li a day; from the fourth month until the seventh month of autumn he at last reached Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 乃溯河西上。

translations.literal: He then went upstream along the west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: From there he pushed upstream along the western bank.

sentences.zh: 魏主以河南四鎮兵少，命諸軍悉收眾北渡。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler, because the four garrisons south of the Yellow River had few troops, ordered all armies to gather their forces and cross north.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the four garrisons south of the Yellow River understrength, the Wei emperor ordered every command to withdraw north across the river.

sentences.zh: 戊子，魏碻磝戍兵棄城去。

translations.literal: On wuzi the Wei garrison at Qiao'ao abandoned the city and left.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the Wei garrison at Qiao'ao abandoned the city.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，滑台戍兵亦去。

translations.literal: On wuxu the Huatai garrison troops also left.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the garrison at Huatai withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 庚子，魏主以大鴻臚陽平公杜超為都督冀、定、相三州諸軍事、太宰，進爵陽平王，鎮鄴，為諸軍節度。

translations.literal: On gengzi the Wei ruler made Grandee of Splendid Happiness Duke Yangping Du Chao commander of all military affairs of the three provinces Ji, Ding, and Xiang, Grand Preceptor, advanced in rank to King of Yangping, stationed at Ye to coordinate all armies.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the Wei emperor made Grandee of Splendid Happiness Duke Yangping Du Chao commander of Ji, Ding, and Xiang, promoted him to King of Yangping and Grand Preceptor, and stationed him at Ye to direct the armies.

sentences.zh: 超，密太后之兄也。

translations.literal: Chao was an elder brother of Empress Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chao was an elder brother of Empress Mi.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，魏洛陽、虎牢戍兵皆棄城去。

translations.literal: On gengxu the Wei garrisons at Luoyang and Hulao all abandoned their cities and left.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the Wei garrisons at Luoyang and Hulao abandoned their posts.

sentences.zh: 到彥之留朱修之守滑台，尹沖守虎牢，建武將軍杜驥守金墉。

translations.literal: Dao Yanzhi left Zhu Xiuzhi to hold Huatai, Yin Chong to hold Hulao, and General Who Establishes Martial Prowess Du Ji to hold Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Yanzhi left Zhu Xiuzhi at Huatai, Yin Chong at Hulao, and General Who Establishes Martial Prowess Du Ji at Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 驥，預之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Ji was a great-great-grandson of Du Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ji was a great-great-grandson of Du Yu.

sentences.zh: 諸軍進頓靈昌津，列守南岸，至於潼關。

translations.literal: The armies advanced and encamped at Lingchang Ford, arrayed to guard the south bank, reaching as far as Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced to Lingchang Ford and lined the south bank all the way to Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 於是司、袞既平，諸軍皆喜，王仲德獨有憂色，曰：「請賢不諳北土情偽，必墮其計。

translations.literal: Thereupon, since Si and Yan provinces were already pacified, all the armies rejoiced; Wang Zhongde alone wore a look of worry and said: "Your sagely worthies do not understand the true and false of the northern lands — you will surely fall into their stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: With Si and Yan provinces seemingly secure, the commanders exulted — only Wang Zhongde looked grim. "Your worthies do not know the north," he said. "You are walking into a trap.

sentences.zh: 胡虜雖仁義不足，而凶狡有餘，今斂戍北歸，必並力完聚。

translations.literal: The barbarian invaders, though deficient in benevolence and righteousness, have abundance of ferocity and cunning; now they are gathering garrisons and returning north — they will surely combine strength and make ready.
translations.idiomatic: The northerners may lack virtue, but they are cunning. Withdraw the garrisons and they will mass their strength.

sentences.zh: 若河冰既合，將復南來，豈可不以為憂乎！」

translations.literal: If the river ice has joined, they will again come south — how can this not be a matter of worry!"
translations.idiomatic: When the river freezes, they will come south again — should we not fear that?"

sentences.zh: 甲寅，林邑王范陽邁遣使入貢，自陳與交州不睦，乞蒙恕宥。

translations.literal: On jiayin the King of Linyi Fan Yangmai sent envoys to submit tribute, declaring himself at odds with Jiao Province and begging to be pardoned and spared.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin King Fan Yangmai of Linyi sent tribute, pleaded that he was at odds with Jiao Province, and asked to be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 八月，魏主遣冠軍將軍安頡督護諸軍，擊到彥之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Wei ruler sent General Who Establishes Martial Supremacy An Rui to supervise and protect all armies and attack Dao Yanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Wei emperor sent General Who Establishes Martial Supremacy An Rui to command the armies against Dao Yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，彥之遣裨將吳興姚聳夫渡河攻冶板，與頡戰；

translations.literal: On bingyin Yanzhi sent Assistant General Yao Songfu of Wuxing to cross the river and attack Yebai; he fought with Rui;
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Dao Yanzhi sent Assistant General Yao Songfu of Wuxing across the river to assault Yebai and engage An Rui;

sentences.zh: 聳夫兵敗，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Songfu's army was defeated; the dead were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Songfu was routed and his losses were heavy.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，魏主遣征西大將軍長孫道生會丹陽王大毘屯河上以御彥之。

translations.literal: On wuyin the Wei ruler sent Grand General Who Conquers the West Changsun Daosheng to join Prince Danyang Da Pi encamped on the river to resist Yanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the Wei emperor sent Grand General Who Conquers the West Changsun Daosheng to join Prince Danyang Da Pi on the river against Dao Yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 燕太祖寢疾，召中書監申秀、侍中陽哲於內殿，屬以後事。

translations.literal: The Yan Founding Emperor lay ill in bed; he summoned Palace Director Shen Xiu and Palace Attendant Yang Zhe to the inner hall and entrusted them with affairs after his death.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor of Northern Yan fell gravely ill; he summoned Palace Director Shen Xiu and Palace Attendant Yang Zhe to the inner hall and entrusted them with the succession.

sentences.zh: 九月，病甚，輦而臨軒，命太子翼攝國事，勒兵聽政，以備非常。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, his illness severe, he was carried in a palanquin to attend at the front hall; he ordered Crown Prince Yi to take charge of state affairs, mustered troops to attend court, to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, desperately ill, he was borne to the throne hall, ordered Crown Prince Yi to govern in his stead, and mobilized the guard against emergency.

sentences.zh: 宋夫人欲立其子受居，惡翼聽政，謂翼曰：「上疾將瘳，奈何遽欲代父臨天下乎！」

translations.literal: Lady Song wished to establish her son Shouju; she hated Yi's attending to government and said to Yi: "The sovereign's illness will soon be cured — why do you so hastily wish to replace your father and preside over all under Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Song wanted her son Shouju on the throne and resented Yi's regency. She told Yi, "Your father's illness is nearly cured — why are you so eager to seize the throne?"

sentences.zh: 翼性仁弱，遂還東宮，日三往省疾。

translations.literal: Yi by nature was benevolent and weak; he then returned to the Eastern Palace and went three times daily to inquire after the illness.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and yielding by nature, Yi withdrew to the Eastern Palace and visited his father three times a day.

sentences.zh: 宋夫人矯詔絕內外，遣閽寺傳問而已，翼及諸子、大臣並不得見，唯中給事胡福獨得出入，專掌禁衛。

translations.literal: Lady Song forged an edict cutting off inner and outer; she sent gatekeepers to convey inquiries only — Yi and all the sons and great ministers alike could not see him; only Central Attendant of the Palace Hu Fu alone could enter and leave, exclusively controlling the forbidden guard.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Song forged an edict sealing the palace; only gate eunuchs passed messages. Yi, the other princes, and the ministers were all shut out — only Central Attendant Hu Fu came and went freely, commanding the guard.

sentences.zh: 福慮宋夫人遂成其謀，乃言於司徒、錄尚書事、中山公弘，弘與壯士數十人被甲入禁中，宿衛皆不戰而散。

translations.literal: Fu feared Lady Song would carry out her plot; he then spoke to Minister-over-the-Masses and Recorder of Affairs of the Imperial Secretariat Duke of Zhongshan Hong; Hong with several dozen stalwarts donned armor and entered the forbidden palace; the night guard all dispersed without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Lady Song would succeed, Hu Fu warned Minister-over-the-Masses Duke of Zhongshan Hong; Hong entered the palace with several dozen armed men, and the guards melted away without a fight.

sentences.zh: 宋夫人命閉東閤，弘家僮庫斗頭勁捷有勇力，逾閤而入，至於皇堂，射殺女御一人。

translations.literal: Lady Song ordered the eastern gate closed; Hong's household slave Koudoutou was agile and possessed of courage and strength; he vaulted the gate and entered, reaching the imperial hall and shooting dead one lady-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Song ordered the eastern gate barred, but Hong's household slave Koudoutou — quick and fierce — vaulted the gate, reached the imperial hall, and shot a lady-in-waiting dead.

sentences.zh: 太祖驚懼而殂。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor was startled and fearful and died.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor died in shock and terror.

sentences.zh: 弘遂即天王位，遣人巡城告曰：「天降凶禍，大行崩背，太子不侍疾，群公不奔喪，疑有逆謀，社稷將危。

translations.literal: Hong then immediately assumed the title of Heavenly King; he sent men to patrol the city and proclaim: "Heaven sends dire calamity; the late sovereign has passed; the crown prince did not attend the illness, the lords did not rush to mourning — there is suspected treason; the altars of state will be imperiled.
translations.idiomatic: Hong seized the throne as Heavenly King and sent criers through the city: "Heaven has sent disaster — the late emperor is dead, yet the crown prince did not attend him and the lords did not come to mourn. Treason is suspected and the realm is in peril.

sentences.zh: 吾備介弟之親，遂攝大位以寧國家，百官叩門入者，進陛二等。」

translations.literal: I as a close younger brother have therefore taken the great throne to settle the state; officials who knock and enter will advance two ranks in rank."
translations.idiomatic: As his younger brother I have taken the throne to save the state. Officials who enter at my gate will rise two ranks."

sentences.zh: 太子翼帥東宮兵出戰而敗，兵皆潰去，弘遣使賜翼死。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yi led Eastern Palace troops out to battle and was defeated; the troops all broke and fled; Hong sent envoys to grant Yi death.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yi marched out with the Eastern Palace guard and was routed; Hong sent orders for his death.

sentences.zh: 太祖有子百餘人，弘皆殺之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor had more than a hundred sons; Hong killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor had more than a hundred sons; Hong killed every one.

sentences.zh: 謚太祖民皇帝，長谷陵。

translations.literal: He gave the posthumous title Civil Emperor to the Founding Emperor; buried at Changgu Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously titled the Founding Emperor Civil Emperor and buried him at Changgu Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 己丑，夏主遣其弟謂以代伐魏鄜城，魏平西將軍始平公隗歸等擊之，殺萬餘人，謂以代遁去。

translations.literal: On jichou the Xia ruler sent his younger brother Wei Yidai to attack Fucheng in Wei; Wei's General Who Pacifies the West Duke of Shiping Kui Gui and others attacked them, killed more than ten thousand men, and Wei Yidai fled away.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the Xia ruler sent his brother Wei Yidai against Fucheng; Wei's General Who Pacifies the West Duke of Shiping Kui Gui crushed the attack, killed more than ten thousand, and Yidai fled.

sentences.zh: 夏主自將數萬人邀擊隗歸於鄜城東，留其弟上谷公社干、廣陽公度洛孤守平涼，遣使來求和，約合兵滅魏，遙分河北：自恆山以東屬宋，以西屬夏。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler personally led several tens of thousands to intercept and attack Kui Gui east of Fucheng; he left his younger brothers Duke of Shanggu Shegan and Duke of Guangyang Duluo'gu to hold Pingliang; he sent envoys to seek peace, agreeing to combine armies to destroy Wei and partition north of the river at a distance: from Mount Heng east would belong to Liu Song, west to Xia.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler personally led tens of thousands to ambush Kui Gui east of Fucheng, left his brothers Duke of Shanggu Shegan and Duke of Guangyang Duluo'gu at Pingliang, and sent envoys proposing an alliance against Wei — east of Mount Heng for Liu Song, west for Xia.

sentences.zh: 魏主聞之，治兵，將伐夏，群臣鹹曰：「劉義隆兵猶在河中，捨之西行，前寇未可必克，而義隆乘虛濟河，則失山東矣。」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler heard of this, marshaled troops, and was about to attack Xia; the ministers all said: "Liu Yilong's troops are still in the river region; if we abandon them and go west, the earlier enemy cannot be surely overcome, and Yilong will seize the opportunity to cross the river — then we will lose the lands east of the mountains."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor mustered troops to strike Xia, but his ministers warned: "Liu Yilong's army is still on the river. Turn west before the Xia are surely beaten, and Yilong will cross the gap — we will lose everything east of the mountains."

sentences.zh: 魏主以問崔浩，對曰：「義隆與赫連定遙相招引，以虛聲唱和，共大國，義隆望定進，定徒義隆前，皆莫敢先入；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler asked Cui Hao; he replied: "Yilong and Helian Ding call to each other from afar, echoing empty threats to intimidate the great state; Yilong waits for Ding to advance, Ding only urges Yilong forward — neither dares enter first;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor asked Cui Hao, who answered: "Yilong and Helian Ding shout threats across the distance to bluff us. Yilong waits for Ding to move; Ding only pushes Yilong ahead — neither will go first.

sentences.zh: 譬如連雞，不得俱飛，無能為害也。

translations.literal: It is like chickens tied together — they cannot both fly; they can do no harm.
translations.idiomatic: They are like chickens tied together — neither can take wing. They pose no real threat.

sentences.zh: 臣始謂義隆軍來，當屯止河中，兩道北上，東道向冀州，西道沖鄴，如此，則陛下當自討之，不得徐行。

translations.literal: I at first supposed Yilong's army coming would encamp and halt in the river region, with two routes going north — the eastern route toward Ji Province, the western route striking Ye — in that case Your Majesty should personally attack them and could not proceed at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: I once feared Yilong would halt on the river and strike north in two columns — east toward Ji Province, west against Ye — forcing Your Majesty to meet him in person without delay.

sentences.zh: 今則不然，東西列兵徑二千里，一處不過數千，形分勢弱。

translations.literal: Now it is not so — east and west they array troops spanning two thousand li; at any one place there are no more than several thousand; form is divided and momentum weak.
translations.idiomatic: But that is not what is happening. His forces stretch two thousand li east to west, a few thousand men here and there — divided and weak.

sentences.zh: 以此觀之，儜兒情見，此不過欲固河自守，無北渡意也。

translations.literal: Viewed in this way, the tender boy's intent is plain — this is nothing but wishing to secure the river and hold on self-defense; there is no intent to cross north.
translations.idiomatic: It is plain the boy only means to hold the river line. He has no appetite to cross north.

sentences.zh: 赫連定殘根易摧，擬之必僕。

translations.literal: Helian Ding's withered root is easy to break; matched against him he will surely fall prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Ding is a broken stump — strike him and he will topple.

sentences.zh: 克定之後，東出潼關，席捲而前，則威震南極，江、淮以北無立草矣。

translations.literal: After conquering Ding, go east out of Tong Pass and sweep forward — then prestige will shake the southern pole; north of the Yangzi and Huai not a blade of standing grass will remain.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ding is crushed, march east through Tong Pass and roll forward — your prestige will shake the south, and nothing will stand north of the Yangzi and Huai.

sentences.zh: 聖策獨發，非愚近所及，願陛下勿疑。」

translations.literal: Your sage strategy alone unfolds — this is not what the foolish and near can reach; I wish Your Majesty not to doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Only Your Majesty's sagacity sees this far. Doubt no longer."

sentences.zh: 甲辰，魏主如統萬，遂襲平涼，以衛兵將軍王斤鎮蒲板。

translations.literal: On jiachen the Wei ruler went to Tongwan and then raided Pingliang; he made Guard General Wang Jin garrison Puban.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the Wei emperor marched on Tongwan and struck Pingliang, leaving Guard General Wang Jin at Puban.

sentences.zh: 斤，建之子也。

translations.literal: Jin was a son of Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin was a son of Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 秦自正月不雨，至於九月，民流叛者甚眾。

translations.literal: In Qin from the first month there was no rain until the ninth month; among the people those who fled and rebelled were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Western Qin saw no rain from the first month through the ninth; refugees and rebels filled the land.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，以竟陵王義宣為南徐州策史，獨戍石頭。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Prince of Jingling Yixuan was made Governor of Southern Xuzhou, alone garrisoning Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Prince of Jingling Yixuan was made Governor of Southern Xuzhou and left alone to hold Shitou.

sentences.zh: 戊午，立錢署，鑄四銖錢。

translations.literal: On wuwu a Mint Office was established and four-zhu coins were cast.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the court established a mint and cast four-zhu coins.

sentences.zh: 到彥之、王仲德沿河置守，還保東平。

translations.literal: Dao Yanzhi and Wang Zhongde set guards along the river and withdrew to hold Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Yanzhi and Wang Zhongde posted guards along the river and fell back to defend Dongping.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，魏安頡自委粟津濟河，攻金墉。

translations.literal: On yihai, An Rui of Wei crossed the river from Weisu Ford and attacked Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Wei's An Rui crossed the river at Weisu Ford and assaulted Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 金墉城不治既久，又無糧食。

translations.literal: Jinyong city had long gone without repair, and moreover had no grain.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyong had long fallen into disrepair and had no supplies.

sentences.zh: 杜驥欲棄城走，恐獲罪。

translations.literal: Du Ji wished to abandon the city and flee, but feared punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ji wanted to abandon the city and flee but feared he would be punished.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖滅秦，遷其鐘虡於江南，有大鐘沒於洛水，帝使姚聳夫將千五百人往取之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Founding Emperor destroyed Qin and moved its bells and bell-frames to the south of the Yangtze; a great bell had sunk in the Luo River, and the emperor sent Yao Songfu with fifteen hundred men to retrieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Founding Emperor conquered Qin, the bells and bell-frames had been moved south of the Yangtze; one great bell had sunk in the Luo River, and the emperor had sent Yao Songfu with fifteen hundred men to recover it.

sentences.zh: 驥紿之曰：「金墉城已修完，糧食亦足，所乏者人耳。

translations.literal: Ji deceived him, saying: "Jinyong city has already been fully repaired and the grain is also sufficient; what it lacks is only men.
translations.idiomatic: Ji deceived him, saying: "Jinyong has been fully repaired and well provisioned; all it lacks is men.

sentences.zh: 今虜騎南渡，當相與並力御之。

translations.literal: Now the enemy horsemen are crossing south; we should join forces to resist them together.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy cavalry are crossing south now; we should stand together and fight them off.

sentences.zh: 大功既立，牽鐘未晚。」

translations.literal: Once the great achievement is established, hauling the bell will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Once we have won this fight, there will still be time to haul up the bell."

sentences.zh: 聳夫從之。

translations.literal: Songfu followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Songfu agreed.

sentences.zh: 既至，見城不可守，乃引去，遂南遁。

translations.literal: When they arrived and saw the city could not be held, they withdrew and then fled south.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived and saw the city was indefensible, they withdrew and fled south.

sentences.zh: 丙子，安頡拔洛陽，殺將士五千餘人。

translations.literal: On bingzi, An Rui took Luoyang and killed more than five thousand officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, An Rui captured Luoyang and killed more than five thousand defenders.

sentences.zh: 杜驥歸，言於帝曰：「本欲以死固守，姚聳夫及城遽走，人情沮敗，不可復禁。」

translations.literal: Du Ji returned and told the emperor: "I originally intended to hold firm even unto death, but Yao Songfu reached the city and fled at once; morale collapsed and could no longer be restrained."
translations.idiomatic: Du Ji returned and told the emperor: "I had meant to hold the city even unto death, but when Yao Songfu arrived he fled at once; morale collapsed beyond recall."

sentences.zh: 上大怒，誅聳夫於壽陽。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and executed Songfu at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and had Songfu executed at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 聳夫勇健，諸偏裨莫及也。

translations.literal: Songfu was brave and strong; none of the assistant generals could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Songfu had been brave and strong—none of the subordinate officers could match him.

sentences.zh: 魏河北諸軍會於七女津。

translations.literal: The Wei armies north of the river assembled at Qinv Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's armies north of the Yellow River gathered at Qinv Ford.

sentences.zh: 到彥之恐其南渡，遣裨將王蟠龍溯流奪其船，杜超等擊斬之。

translations.literal: Dao Yanzhi, fearing they would cross south, sent Assistant General Wang Panlong upstream to seize their boats; Du Chao and others attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful of a southern crossing, Dao Yanzhi sent Assistant General Wang Panlong upstream to seize their boats; Du Chao and others struck and killed him.

sentences.zh: 安頡與龍驤將軍陸俟進攻虎牢，辛巳，拔之；

translations.literal: An Rui and General of the Flying Dragon Lu Si advanced to attack Hulao; on xinsi, they took it;
translations.idiomatic: An Rui and General of the Flying Dragon Lu Si attacked Hulao; on xinsi they captured it;

sentences.zh: 尹沖及滎陽太守清河崔模降魏。

translations.literal: Yin Chong and Cui Mo of Qinghe, Administrator of Xingyang, surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chong and Xingyang Administrator Cui Mo of Qinghe surrendered to Wei.

sentences.zh: 秦王暮末為河西所逼，遣其臣王愷、烏訥闐請迎於魏，魏人許以平涼、安定封之。

translations.literal: King Muemo of Qin, pressed by Hexi, sent his ministers Wang Kai and Wu Nedian to ask Wei to receive him; the Wei people promised to enfeoff him with Pingliang and Anding.
translations.idiomatic: King Muemo of Qin, hard pressed by Hexi, sent ministers Wang Kai and Wu Nedian to ask Wei to receive him; Wei promised to enfeoff him with Pingliang and Anding.

sentences.zh: 暮末乃焚城邑，毀寶器，帥戶萬五千，東如上邽。

translations.literal: Muemo then burned the cities and towns, destroyed precious vessels, and led fifteen thousand households east toward Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Muemo burned his towns, smashed his treasures, and led fifteen thousand households east toward Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 至高田谷，給事黃門侍郎郭恆謀劫詛興國以叛；

translations.literal: When they reached Gaotian Valley, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Guo Heng plotted to seize and abduct Xingguo to rebel;
translations.idiomatic: At Gaotian Valley, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Guo Heng plotted to seize Prince Xingguo and rebel;

sentences.zh: 事覺，暮末殺之。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered, Muemo killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered and Muemo had him killed.

sentences.zh: 夏主聞暮末將至，發兵拒之。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler heard Muemo was coming and sent troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Muemo was approaching, the Xia ruler sent troops to block him.

sentences.zh: 暮末留保南安，其故地皆入於吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Muemo remained to hold Nan'an; his former territory all fell to Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Muemo held Nan'an while his former lands all passed to Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙酉，魏主至平涼，夏上谷公社乾等嬰城固守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yiyou, the Wei emperor reached Pingliang; Gongshe Gan of Shanggu of Xia and others relied on the city and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yiyou, the Wei emperor reached Pingliang; Gongshe Gan of Shanggu and other Xia commanders barricaded themselves in the city.

sentences.zh: 魏主使赫連昌招之，不下，乃使安西將軍古弼等將兵趣安定。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor sent Helian Chang to summon them; they did not submit, so he sent General Who Pacifies the West Gu Bi and others with troops to hurry to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor sent Helian Chang to negotiate their surrender; when they refused, he sent General Who Pacifies the West Gu Bi toward Anding.

sentences.zh: 夏主自鄜城還安定，將步騎二萬北救平涼，與弼遇，弼偽退以誘之；

translations.literal: The Xia ruler returned from Fucheng to Anding and led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry north to rescue Pingliang; meeting Bi, Bi feigned retreat to lure him;
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler left Fucheng for Anding and marched twenty thousand foot and horse north to relieve Pingliang; Gu Bi met him and feigned retreat to draw him on;

sentences.zh: 夏主追之，魏主使高車馳擊之，夏兵大敗，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler pursued; the Wei emperor sent the Gaoche to charge and strike them; the Xia army was greatly defeated and several thousand heads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler pursued; the Wei emperor sent Gaoche cavalry in a charge; the Xia army was routed and thousands were slain.

sentences.zh: 夏主還走，登鶉觚原，為方陣以自固，魏兵就圍之。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler turned and fled, ascended Yunqiu Plain, formed a square formation to secure himself, and the Wei troops came and besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler fled back up onto Yunqiu Plain, formed a square battle line, and the Wei armies closed in around him.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，加征南大將軍檀道濟都督征討諸軍事，帥眾伐魏。

translations.literal: On renchen, Tan Daoji, General Who Destroys the South, was further appointed Commander of All Affairs of the Punitive Campaign and led troops to attack Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, General Who Destroys the South Tan Daoji was made supreme commander of the punitive campaign and marched against Wei.

sentences.zh: 甲午，魏壽光侯叔孫建、汝陰公長孫道生濟河而南。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Shusun Jian, Marquis of Shouguang, and Changsun Daosheng, Duke of Ruyin, crossed the river and went south.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Marquis of Shouguang Shusun Jian and Duke of Ruyin Changsun Daosheng crossed the river southward.

sentences.zh: 到彥之聞洛陽、虎牢不守，諸軍相繼奔敗，欲引兵還。

translations.literal: Dao Yanzhi heard that Luoyang and Hulao were not held and that the armies had one after another fled in defeat; he wished to withdraw his troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Dao Yanzhi learned that Luoyang and Hulao had fallen and the armies were collapsing in flight, he wanted to pull back.

sentences.zh: 殿中將軍垣護之以書諫之，以為宜使竺靈秀朱修之守滑台，自帥大軍進擬河北，且曰：「昔人有連年攻戰，失眾乏糧，猶張膽爭前，莫肯輕退。

translations.literal: Palace General Yuan Huzhi remonstrated with him in a letter, holding that Zhu Lingxiu and Zhu Xiuzhi should be left to hold Huatai while he himself led the main army forward toward Hebei, and said: "In former times there were men who fought year after year, losing troops and running short of grain, yet still dared to press forward and would not lightly retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Palace General Yuan Huzhi wrote to dissuade him, arguing that Zhu Lingxiu and Zhu Xiuzhi should hold Huatai while he led the main force toward Hebei, adding: "Men have fought for years, losing troops and starving, yet still pressed forward and refused to withdraw lightly.

sentences.zh: 況今青州豐穰，濟漕流通，士馬飽逸，威力無損。

translations.literal: Moreover, now Qing Province is rich with harvest, transport on the Ji is open, men and horses are well fed and rested, and fighting strength is undiminished.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Province is rich this year, grain moves freely on the Ji, our men and horses are fed and rested, and our strength is undiminished.

sentences.zh: 若空棄滑台，坐喪成業，豈朝廷受任之旨邪！」

translations.literal: If you empty Huatai for nothing and sit by while the achievement is lost, how can that accord with the court's intent in appointing you!"
translations.idiomatic: To abandon Huatai for nothing and throw away everything we have won—how can that be what the court intended when it entrusted you with this command!"

sentences.zh: 彥之不從。

translations.literal: Yanzhi did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi ignored him.

sentences.zh: 護之，苗之子也。

translations.literal: Huzhi was the son of Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Huzhi was the son of Yuan Miao.

sentences.zh: 彥之欲焚舟步走，王仲德曰：「洛陽既陷，虎牢不守，自然之勢也。

translations.literal: Yanzhi wished to burn the boats and withdraw on foot; Wang Zhongde said: "Luoyang has already fallen and Hulao is not held—this is the natural course of things.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi wanted to burn the boats and retreat overland; Wang Zhongde said: "Luoyang is lost and Hulao has fallen—that is only to be expected.

sentences.zh: 今虜去我猶千里，滑台尚有強兵，若遽捨舟南走，士卒必散。

translations.literal: Now the enemy is still a thousand li from us, and Huatai still has strong troops; if we abruptly abandon the boats and flee south, the soldiers will surely scatter.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is still a thousand li away, and Huatai still holds strong forces; if we abandon the boats and run south at once, the army will disintegrate.

sentences.zh: 當引舟入濟，至馬耳谷口，吏詳所宜。」

translations.literal: We should bring the boats into the Ji, reach the mouth of Ma'er Valley, and have the officers carefully deliberate what course is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Sail into the Ji, reach the mouth of Ma'er Valley, and then carefully decide what course to take from there."

sentences.zh: 彥之先有目疾，至是大動；

translations.literal: Yanzhi had had an eye ailment earlier; on this occasion it flared severely;
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi had long suffered from an eye ailment, and now it worsened sharply;

sentences.zh: 且將士疾疫，乃引兵自清入濟。

translations.literal: moreover the officers and soldiers were afflicted with epidemic illness, so he led the army from the Qing into the Ji.
translations.idiomatic: and his troops were ravaged by plague; he led them from the Qing into the Ji.

sentences.zh: 南至歷城，焚舟棄甲，步趨彭城。

translations.literal: Going south to Licheng, they burned the boats, cast off their armor, and marched on foot toward Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached Licheng they had burned their boats, cast off their armor, and were hurrying on foot toward Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 竺靈秀棄須昌，南奔湖陸，表、袞大擾。

translations.literal: Zhu Lingxiu abandoned Xuchang and fled south to Huluo; Qing and Yan provinces were greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lingxiu abandoned Xuchang and fled south to Huluo; Qing and Yan provinces were thrown into chaos.

sentences.zh: 長沙王義欣在彭城，將佐恐魏兵大至，勸義欣委鎮還都，義欣不從。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changsha Yixin was at Pengcheng; his officers and aides, fearing the Wei armies would arrive in force, urged Yixin to abandon his post and return to the capital, but Yixin would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Changsha Yixin was at Pengcheng; his staff, fearing a major Wei advance, urged him to abandon the garrison and return to the capital, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 魏兵攻濟南，濟南太守武進蕭承之帥數百人拒之。

translations.literal: Wei troops attacked Jinan; Xiao Chengzhi of Wujin, Administrator of Jinan, led several hundred men to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei forces attacked Jinan; Jinan Administrator Xiao Chengzhi of Wujin led several hundred men to hold them off.

sentences.zh: 魏眾大集，承之使偃兵，開城門。

translations.literal: The Wei host gathered in great numbers; Chengzhi had his troops lay down their arms and opened the city gates.
translations.idiomatic: As the Wei host massed, Chengzhi ordered his men to stand down and opened the city gates.

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「賊眾我寡，奈何輕敵之甚！」

translations.literal: The men said: "The bandits are many and we are few—why treat the enemy so lightly!"
translations.idiomatic: His men cried: "The enemy outnumber us—why show them such contempt!"

sentences.zh: 承之曰：「今懸守窮城，事已危急，若復示弱，必為所屠，唯當見強以待之耳。」

translations.literal: Chengzhi said: "Now we hold a desperate city in isolation and the situation is already critical; if we show weakness again, we will surely be slaughtered—we can only appear strong and wait for them."
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi replied: "We are trapped in a doomed town and the crisis is acute; if we show weakness now we are finished—we must look strong and wait them out."

sentences.zh: 魏人疑有伏兵，遂引去。

translations.literal: The Wei men suspected an ambush and therefore withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei troops suspected an ambush and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 魏軍圍夏主數日，斷其水草，人馬飢渴。

translations.literal: The Wei army besieged the Xia ruler for several days, cutting off his fodder and water; men and horses were hungry and thirsty.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei armies besieged the Xia ruler for days, cutting off fodder and water until men and horses were starving and parched.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，夏主引眾下鶉觚原。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the Xia ruler led his host down from Yunqiu Plain.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, the Xia ruler led his troops down from Yunqiu Plain.

sentences.zh: 魏武衛將軍丘眷擊之，夏眾大潰，死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Qiu Juan, General of the Martial Guard of Wei, struck them; the Xia host was greatly routed and more than ten thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Martial Guard Qiu Juan struck them; the Xia army collapsed and more than ten thousand were killed.

sentences.zh: 夏主中重創，單騎走，收其餘眾，驅民五萬，西保上邽。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler was struck by a grave wound, fled alone on horseback, gathered his remaining host, and drove fifty thousand civilians west to hold Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler was badly wounded, fled alone on horseback, rallied his survivors, and drove fifty thousand civilians west to Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 魏人獲夏主之弟丹陽公烏視拔、武陵公禿骨及公侯以下百餘人。

translations.literal: The Wei men captured the Xia ruler's younger brothers Wushiba, Duke of Danyang, and Tugu, Duke of Wuling, along with more than a hundred nobles and officials.
translations.idiomatic: Wei captured the Xia ruler's brothers Wushiba, Duke of Danyang, and Tugu, Duke of Wuling, along with more than a hundred nobles and officials.

sentences.zh: 是日，魏兵乘勝進攻安定，夏東平公乙斗棄城奔長安，驅略數千家，西奔上邽。

translations.literal: That same day the Wei troops pressed their victory to attack Anding; Yidou, Prince of Dongping of Xia, abandoned the city and fled to Chang'an, driving off and plundering several thousand households before fleeing west to Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the Wei armies pressed on to Anding; Prince of Dongping Yidou abandoned the city for Chang'an, then drove off several thousand households and fled west to Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，魏叔孫建攻竺靈秀於湖陸，靈秀大敗，死者五千餘人。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Shusun Jian of Wei attacked Zhu Lingxiu at Huluo; Lingxiu was greatly defeated and more than five thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Shusun Jian attacked Zhu Lingxiu at Huluo; Lingxiu was routed and more than five thousand were killed.

sentences.zh: 建還頓城。

translations.literal: Jian returned and encamped at the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jian withdrew and encamped at the city.

sentences.zh: 己亥，魏主如安定。

translations.literal: On jihai, the Wei emperor went to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, the Wei emperor went to Anding.

sentences.zh: 庚子，還，臨平涼，掘塹圍之。

translations.literal: On gengzi he returned, came to Pingliang, dug trenches, and besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi he returned to Pingliang, dug trenches, and laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 安慰初附，赦秦、雍之民，賜覆七年。

translations.literal: To comfort those newly submitted, he pardoned the people of Qin and Yong and granted seven years' remission of cloth levies.
translations.idiomatic: To reassure the newly submitted, he pardoned the people of Qin and Yong and remitted cloth levies for seven years.

sentences.zh: 夏隴西守將降魏。

translations.literal: The Xia garrison commander of Longxi surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia commander of Longxi surrendered to Wei.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，魏安頡督諸軍攻滑台。

translations.literal: On xinchou, An Rui of Wei supervised all armies in attacking Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, An Rui of Wei took command of the armies and assaulted Huatai.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜遣尚書郎宗舒等入貢於魏，魏主與之宴，執崔浩之手以示舒等曰：「汝所聞崔公，此則是也。

translations.literal: King Mengsun of Hexi sent Attendant Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Zong Shu and others to present tribute to Wei; the Wei emperor feasted with them, took Cui Hao by the hand, and showed him to Shu and the others, saying: "The Lord Cui of whom you have heard—this is he.
translations.idiomatic: King Mengsun of Hexi sent Masters of Writing Attendant Gentleman Zong Shu and others to pay tribute at Wei; the Wei emperor held a feast, took Cui Hao by the hand, and showed him to the envoys, saying: "The Lord Cui you have heard so much about—here he is.

sentences.zh: 才略之美，於今無比。

translations.literal: In talent and strategy he is unmatched in our age.
translations.idiomatic: In talent and strategy he has no equal today.

sentences.zh: 朕動止咨之，豫陳成敗，若合符契，未嘗失也。」

translations.literal: In every move I consult him; he foretells success and failure, and it matches as though by tally—never once has he missed."
translations.idiomatic: I consult him in every decision; he foretells outcomes as though reading a tally, and has never once been wrong."

sentences.zh: 魏以叔孫建都督冀、青等四州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Shusun Jian Commander of the Military Affairs of Ji, Qing, and four other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made Shusun Jian commander of the armies of Ji, Qing, and four other provinces.

sentences.zh: 魏尚書庫結帥騎五千迎秦王暮末。

translations.literal: Kujie, a Master of Writing of Wei, led five thousand horsemen to welcome King Muemo of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Master of Writing Kujie led five thousand cavalry to welcome King Muemo of Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦衛將軍吉毘以為不宜內徙，暮末從之，庫結引還。

translations.literal: Ji Bi, General of the Guard of Qin, held that an inward move was inadvisable; Muemo followed his view and Kujie withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's General of the Guard Ji Bi argued that moving inland was unwise; Muemo agreed and Kujie withdrew.

sentences.zh: 南安諸羌萬餘人叛秦，推安南將軍、督八郡諸軍事、廣寧太守焦遺為主，遺不從，乃劫遺族子長城護軍亮為主，帥眾攻南安。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand Qiang of Nan'an rebelled against Qin and tried to make Jiao Yi, General Who Pacifies the South, Supervisor of the Military Affairs of Eight Commanderies, and Administrator of Guangning, their leader; Yi refused, so they seized Yi's clansman Liang, Protector of the Army of Changcheng, as leader and led the host to attack Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand Qiang of Nan'an rose against Qin and tried to make General Who Pacifies the South Jiao Yi, supervisor of eight commanderies and Administrator of Guangning, their leader; when Yi refused, they seized his clansman Liang, Protector of the Army at Changcheng, and marched on Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 暮未請救於氐王楊難當，難當遣將軍苻南帥騎三千救之，暮末與之合擊諸羌。

translations.literal: Muemo asked aid from Di King Yang Nandang; Nandang sent General Fu Nan with three thousand horsemen to rescue him, and Muemo joined him in a combined attack on the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Muemo appealed to Di King Yang Nandang, who sent General Fu Nan with three thousand cavalry; Muemo joined him in crushing the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 諸羌潰，亮奔還廣寧，暮未進軍攻之，以手令與焦遺使取亮；

translations.literal: The Qiang were routed; Liang fled back to Guangning; Muemo advanced to attack him and gave Jiao Yi a handwritten order to deliver Liang;
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang broke; Liang fled to Guangning; Muemo marched against him and sent Jiao Yi a handwritten order to produce Liang;

sentences.zh: 十二月遺斬亮者出降，暮末進遺號鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the man who had beheaded Liang came out and surrendered; Muemo advanced Yi to the title General Who Pacifies the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the man who had killed Liang surrendered; Muemo promoted Yi to General Who Pacifies the State.

sentences.zh: 秦略陽太守弘農楊顯以郡降夏。

translations.literal: Yang Xian of Hongnong, Administrator of Lueyang of Qin, surrendered the commandery to Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's Lueyang Administrator Yang Xian of Hongnong surrendered his commandery to Xia.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以長沙王義欣為豫州刺史，鎮壽陽。

translations.literal: On xinyou, the Prince of Changsha Yixin was made Governor of Yuzhou and garrisoned at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Prince of Changsha Yixin was appointed Governor of Yuzhou and posted at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 壽陽土荒民散，城郭頹敗，盜賊公行。

translations.literal: At Shouyang the land was waste, the people scattered, the walls and towers ruined, and bandits walked openly.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyang was a wasteland of ruined walls and scattered people, with bandits roaming openly.

sentences.zh: 義欣隨宜經理，境內安業，道不拾遺，城府完實，遂為盛籓。

translations.literal: Yixin governed as circumstances required; within his borders people settled to their work, no one picked up lost goods on the road, the city walls and offices were made whole and strong, and the region became a great frontier province.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin governed pragmatically; order returned, lost goods went untouched on the roads, the walls and offices were rebuilt, and the region became a flourishing frontier stronghold.

sentences.zh: 芍陂久廢，義欣修治堤防，引河水入陂，溉田萬餘頃，無復旱災。

translations.literal: Quepi had long lain abandoned; Yixin repaired the dikes and embankments, led river water into the reservoir, irrigated more than ten thousand qing of fields, and drought disasters ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The long-neglected Quepi reservoir Yixin restored; he repaired the dikes, fed it with river water, irrigated more than ten thousand qing of fields, and ended the droughts.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，夏上谷公社干、廣陽公度洛孤出降，魏克平涼。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Gongshe Gan of Shanggu of Xia and Duluo Gu, Prince of Guangyang, came out and surrendered; Wei took Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Gongshe Gan of Shanggu and Prince of Guangyang Duluo Gu surrendered; Wei captured Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 關中侯豆代田得奚斤、娥清等，獻於魏主。

translations.literal: Dou Daitian, Marquis of Guanzhong, captured Xi Jin, E Qing, and others and presented them to the Wei emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Guanzhong Dou Daitian captured Xi Jin, E Qing, and others and presented them to the Wei emperor.

sentences.zh: 魏主以夏主之後賜代田，命斤膝行執酒以奉代田，謂斤曰：「全汝生者，代田也。」

translations.literal: The Wei emperor gave Dou Daitian the daughter of the Xia ruler and ordered Jin to go on his knees bearing wine to serve Daitian, saying to Jin: "The one who preserved your life is Daitian."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor gave Dou Daitian a princess of Xia and ordered Jin to kneel and serve him wine, telling Jin: "Dou Daitian is the man who saved your life."

sentences.zh: 賜代田爵井陘侯，加散騎常侍、右衛將軍，領內都幢將。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Daitian as Marquis of Jingxing, added the posts of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of the Right Guard, and made him lead the Inner Capital Standard Bearer.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Daitian as Marquis of Jingxing, made him Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of the Right Guard, and appointed him Inner Capital Standard Bearer.

sentences.zh: 夏長安、臨晉、武功守將皆走，關中悉入於魏。

translations.literal: The Xia garrison commanders of Chang'an, Linjin, and Wugong all fled; all of Guanzhong passed to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia garrison commanders of Chang'an, Linjin, and Wugong all fled; all of Guanzhong fell to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏主留巴東公延普鎮安定，以鎮西將軍王斤鎮長安。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor left Yan Pu, Prince of Badong, to garrison Anding and made Xi Jin, General Who Pacifies the West, garrison Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor left Prince of Badong Yan Pu at Anding and posted General Who Pacifies the West Xi Jin at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 壬申，魏主東還，以奚斤為宰士，使負酒食以從。

translations.literal: On renshen the Wei emperor returned east and made Xi Jin a feast-bearer, having him carry wine and food in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the Wei emperor headed east; he reduced Xi Jin to feast-bearer and made him carry wine and food in his train.

sentences.zh: 王斤驕矜不法，信用左右，調役百姓，民不堪命，南奔漢川者數千家。

translations.literal: Xi Jin was arrogant and lawless, trusting his close attendants, conscripting and taxing the people until they could not bear it; several thousand households fled south to Hanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin grew arrogant and lawless, trusting his favorites and grinding the people with levies until thousands of households fled south to Hanchuan.

sentences.zh: 魏主案治得實，斬斤以徇。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor investigated, found the facts proven, and executed Jin as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor investigated, confirmed the abuses, and had Jin executed as a warning.

sentences.zh: 右將軍到彥之、安北將軍王仲德皆下獄免官，袞州刺史竺靈秀坐棄軍伏誅。

translations.literal: Dao Yanzhi, General of the Right, and Wang Zhongde, General Who Pacifies the North, were both imprisoned and stripped of office; Zhu Lingxiu, Governor of Yanzhou, was executed for abandoning the army.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Right Dao Yanzhi and General Who Pacifies the North Wang Zhongde were imprisoned and dismissed; Yanzhou Governor Zhu Lingxiu was executed for abandoning his command.

sentences.zh: 上見垣護之書而善之，以為北高平太守。

translations.literal: The emperor saw Yuan Huzhi's letter and approved it, appointing him Administrator of Northern Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read Yuan Huzhi's letter with approval and made him Administrator of Northern Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 彥之之北伐也，甲兵資實甚盛；

translations.literal: When Yanzhi marched north, armor, weapons, and supplies were very abundant;
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhi marched north, his army went forth abundantly armed and supplied;

sentences.zh: 乃敗還，委棄蕩盡，府藏、武庫為之空虛。

translations.literal: yet he returned in defeat, having cast away and lost everything; the treasury stores and armory were emptied on his account.
translations.idiomatic: yet he returned in defeat having cast everything away; the treasury and armory were left empty.

sentences.zh: 它日，上與群臣宴，有荒外降人在坐。

translations.literal: Another day the emperor feasted with his ministers, and among those seated was a man who had surrendered from beyond the frontier wilds.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor feasted with his ministers, and a man who had surrendered from beyond the frontier was present.

sentences.zh: 上問尚書庫部郎顧琛：「庫中仗猶有幾許？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Gu Chen, Attendant Gentleman of the Storehouse Section of the Masters of Writing: "How many weapons remain in the storehouse?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Masters of Writing Storehouse Section Attendant Gentleman Gu Chen: "How many weapons remain in the armory?"

sentences.zh: 琛詭對：「有十萬人仗。」

translations.literal: Chen answered deceptively: "There are enough weapons for a hundred thousand men."
translations.idiomatic: Chen answered evasively: "Enough arms for a hundred thousand men."

sentences.zh: 上既問而悔之，得琛對，甚喜。

translations.literal: The emperor, having asked, already regretted it; when he received Chen's answer he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor already regretted asking; Chen's answer delighted him.

sentences.zh: 琛，和之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Chen was the great-grandson of Hezhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was the great-grandson of Gu Hezhi.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康與王弘並錄尚書，義康意猶怏怏，欲得揚州，形於辭旨；

translations.literal: The Prince of Pengcheng Yikang and Wang Hong both served as Masters of Writing in the Secretariat; Yikang's mind was still resentful, for he wanted Yang Province, and this showed in his words;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Yikang and Wang Hong shared the Secretariat; Yikang remained discontented, wanting Yang Province, and his resentment showed in his speech;

sentences.zh: 以弘弟曇首居中，為上所親委，愈不悅。

translations.literal: because Hong's younger brother Tanshou held the central post and was personally entrusted by the emperor, he grew all the more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: and because Hong's brother Tanshou held the central post and enjoyed the emperor's personal trust, he grew all the more bitter.

sentences.zh: 弘以老病，屢乞骸骨，曇首自求吳郡，上皆不許。

translations.literal: Hong, citing age and illness, repeatedly begged to surrender his bones; Tanshou himself asked for Wu Commandery; the emperor refused both.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, pleading age and illness, repeatedly asked to retire; Tanshou sought appointment in Wu Commandery; the emperor refused both.

sentences.zh: 義康謂人曰：「王公久病不起，神州詎宜臥治！」

translations.literal: Yikang said to others: "The royal duke has long been ill and cannot rise—how can the sacred land be governed from bed!"
translations.idiomatic: Yikang told others: "Wang Hong has been bedridden for ages—how can the heartland be run from a sickbed!"

sentences.zh: 曇首勸弘減府中文武之半以授義康，上聽割二千人，義康乃悅。

translations.literal: Tanshou urged Hong to reduce the civil and military staff of his office by half and give it to Yikang; the emperor approved cutting two thousand men, and only then was Yikang pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Tanshou urged Hong to transfer half his civil and military staff to Yikang; the emperor approved two thousand men, and Yikang was finally satisfied.
